translations.text: Without a heading.
Why did the nations rage, and the peoples meditate on empty things?
[?] the kings of the earth; they gathered together [?] against the Lord [?] his Anointed.
Let us tear apart their bonds and cast their yoke away from us.
He who dwells [?] will laugh at him, and the Lord will mock them.
Then he will speak to them in his anger and terrify them in his fury.
But I have been appointed king by him over Zion, his holy mountain,
proclaiming the Lord’s decree. The Lord said to me, “You are my Son; today I have begotten you.
Ask of me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance and the ends of the earth as your possession.
You will shepherd them with an iron rod; you will shatter them like a potter’s vessels.”
And now, kings, understand; be instructed, all who judge the earth.
Serve the Lord with fear, and rejoice in him with trembling.
Accept instruction, lest the Lord become angry and you perish from the righteous path. When his fury flares up quickly, blessed are all who trust in him.
A psalm of David, when he fled from his son Absalom.
Lord, why have those who trouble me multiplied? Many have risen against me. Many have risen against me.
Many say of my soul, “There is no salvation for him in his God.” Interlude.
But you, Lord, are my protector, my glory; you have lifted up my head.
With my voice I cried to the Lord, and he heard me from his holy mountain.
I lay down and slept; I arose, for the Lord will protect me.
I will not fear the countless people who attack me on every side.
Arise, Lord; save me, my God, for you have struck all who are my enemies without cause; you have shattered the teeth of sinners.
Salvation belongs to the Lord, and your blessing is upon your people. Glory.
For the end. A psalm of David.
When I cried out, you heard me, God of my righteousness. In distress you gave me room. Have mercy on me and hear my prayer.
Sons of men, how long will you be hard-hearted? Why do you love empty things and seek falsehood?
And know that the Lord has set apart his faithful one [?]. The Lord will hear me when I cry out to him.
Be angry, but do not sin. For what you say in your hearts, be contrite on your beds.
Offer a sacrifice of righteousness, and put your hope in the Lord.
Many say, “Who will show us good things?” The light of your face has been marked upon us, Lord.
You have put gladness in my heart. They have increased through the yield of their wheat, wine, and oil.
In peace I will both sleep and rest, for you, Lord, have made me dwell alone in hope.
For the end. Concerning her who inherits. A psalm of David.
Listen to my words, Lord; understand my cry.
Listen to the voice of my prayer, my King and my God, for I will pray to you, Lord.
In the morning you will hear my voice. In the morning I will stand before you and look.
For you are not a God who desires lawlessness; an evil person will not dwell with you.
Nor will lawbreakers remain before your eyes. You have hated all who practice lawlessness.
You will destroy all who speak lies. The Lord detests the crooked and deceitful man.
But through the abundance of your mercy I will enter your house. I will bow down toward your holy temple in fear of you [?].
Lord, lead, lead me; lead me in your righteousness because of my enemies. Make my path straight before you.
For there is no truth in their mouths; their heart is empty. Their throat is an open grave; with their tongues they practiced deceit.
Judge them. Let them fall away from their plans. Cast them out because of their many acts of ungodliness, for they have angered you, Lord.
And all who put their hope in you will be glad; they will rejoice forever. You will dwell among them, and those who love your name will boast in you.
For you will bless the righteous person, Lord. You have crowned us with your favor as with a shield.
For the end. With songs. Concerning the eighth. A psalm of David.
Lord, do not rebuke me in your fury or discipline me in your anger.
Have mercy on me, Lord, for I am weak. Heal me, Lord, for my bones are shaken.
And my soul is greatly troubled. But you, Lord—how long?
Turn back, Lord, and deliver my soul. Save me for the sake of your mercy.
For in death there is no one who remembers you. And in Hades, who will give you thanks?
I am worn out with my sighing. Every night I wash my bed; I soak my couch with my tears.
My eye is troubled by anger. I have grown old among all my enemies.
Depart from me, all you who practice lawlessness, for the Lord has heard the sound of my weeping.
The Lord has heard my prayer; the Lord has accepted my supplication.
Let all my enemies be ashamed and troubled. Let them turn back and be utterly ashamed very quickly. Glory.
A psalm of David, which he sang to the Lord concerning the words of Cush, the son of Benjamin.
O Lord my God, I have put my trust in you. Save me from all who pursue me, and deliver me.
Lest he seize my soul like a lion, with no one to deliver or save me.
O Lord my God, if I have done this, if there is injustice in my hands,
if I have repaid with evil those who repay me, then may I fall away from my enemies empty-handed.
Then let the enemy pursue my soul and overtake it; let him trample my life into the ground and lay my glory in the dust.
Rise, O Lord, in your anger; lift yourself up against the fury of your enemies. Arise, O Lord my God, according to the command you have given.
The assembly of peoples will surround you; for their sake return on high.
The Lord will judge the peoples. Judge me, O Lord, according to my righteousness and according to the innocence within me.
Let the wickedness of sinners come to an end, and [?] the righteous, O righteous God, who tests hearts and inward parts.
My help comes from God, who saves the upright in heart.
God is a righteous judge, strong and patient, and he does not bring anger every day.
If you do not turn back, he will sharpen his sword. He has drawn his bow and made it ready.
With it he has prepared instruments of death; he has made his arrows for those who burn.
Look, he has labored to bring forth injustice; he has conceived trouble and given birth to lawlessness.
He dug a pit and hollowed it out, and fell into the hole he had made.
His trouble will return upon his own head, and his injustice will descend upon his own crown.
I will give thanks to the Lord according to his righteousness, and I will sing to the name of the Lord Most High.
For the end. Concerning the winepresses. A psalm of David.
O Lord, our Lord, how wonderful is your name throughout the earth! For your majesty has been raised above the heavens.
From the mouths of infants at the breast you have perfected praise because of your enemies, to destroy the enemy and the avenger.
When I look at the heavens, the work of your fingers, the moon and the stars that you have established,
what is man that you remember him, or the son of man that you care for him?
You have made him a little lower than the angels; you have crowned him with glory and honor.
You have set him over the works of your hands; you have put everything under his feet:
all sheep and oxen, and also the beasts of the field,
the birds of the heavens and the fish of the sea, and whatever passes along the paths of the seas.
O Lord, our Lord, how wonderful is your name throughout the earth!
Glory. [?] For the end. Concerning the hidden things of the son. A psalm of David.
I will praise you, O Lord, with all my heart; I will tell of all your wonders.
I will be glad and rejoice in you; I will sing to your name, O Most High.
When my enemy turns back, they will grow weak and perish before your face.
For you have upheld my judgment and my cause, sitting on the throne and judging with righteousness.
You have rebuked the nations, and the ungodly man has perished; his name will be wiped out forever and ever.
The enemy’s weapons have failed completely, and you have destroyed cities. Their memory has perished with a crash.
But the Lord remains forever; he has prepared his throne for judgment.
He judges the world in righteousness; he will judge the peoples with fairness.
The Lord has become a refuge for the poor, a helper at the right time in troubles.
Let those who know your name trust in you, for you have not abandoned those who seek you, O Lord.
Sing to the Lord who dwells in Zion; proclaim his deeds among the nations.
Interlude. For he who demands an accounting for their blood has remembered; he has not forgotten the cry of the poor.
Have mercy on me, O Lord; see how my enemies have brought me low, you who lift me up from the gates of death,
so that I may proclaim all your praises at the gates of the daughter of Zion. Let us rejoice in your salvation.
The nations have sunk into the destruction they prepared; their foot has been caught in the net they hid.
The Lord is known by the judgments he carries out; the sinner has been caught in the works of his own hands. Interlude.
Sinners will return to hell—all the nations that forget God.
For the needy will not be forgotten forever; the endurance of the poor will not perish forever.
Arise, Lord! Let no mortal prevail; let the nations be judged before you.
Appoint a lawgiver over them, Lord, so that the nations may understand that they are human.
Why, Lord, do you stand far away? Why do you look away when you are needed, in times of trouble?
In the wicked man's arrogance, the needy man is set ablaze. They are caught in the schemes they devise.
For the sinner is praised for his soul's desires, and the wrongdoer is blessed.
The sinner [?] has provoked the Lord. In his great anger he will not seek him out. God is not before his face.
His ways are defiled at all times. Your judgments are removed from his sight. He overcomes all his enemies; he overcomes all his enemies.
For he said in his heart, “I will not be shaken; from generation to generation I will be free from harm.”
His mouth is full of curses, bitterness, and deceit; under his tongue are trouble and suffering.
He sits in ambush with the rich, in secret places, to kill the innocent. His eyes watch the poor.
He lies in wait in secret places like a lion in its enclosure. He lies in wait to seize the needy, to seize the needy and drag him into his net.
He will bring him low. He will crouch and fall when he has gained mastery over the poor.
For he said in his heart, “God has forgotten. He has turned his face away so that he will never see.”
Arise, Lord my God! Let your hand be lifted up. Do not forget your poor forever.
Why has the wicked man provoked God? For he said in his heart, “He will not call me to account.”
You see, for you observe suffering and rage, so that [?]. The needy man is left to you. Be a helper to the orphan.
Crush the arm of the sinful and wicked man. His sin will be sought out and will not be found.
The Lord is king forever and ever. You nations will perish from his land.
The Lord has heard the desire of the poor. Your ear has attended to the readiness of their hearts.
Give justice to the orphan and the lowly, so that no mortal may boast on earth any longer.
For the end. A psalm of David.
In the Lord I have placed my hope. How can you say to my soul, “Fly away to the mountains like a bird”?
A sparrow. For look, the sinners have drawn their bow. They have prepared their arrows in the quiver to shoot in the darkness at the upright in heart.
For they have destroyed what you established. But what has the righteous man done? The Lord is in your holy temple.
The Lord’s throne is in heaven. His eyes look upon the poor; his eyelids examine the sons of men.
The Lord examines the righteous and the ungodly, but whoever loves injustice hates his own soul.
He will rain snares upon sinners. Fire and sulfur and a stormy wind are the portion of their cup.
For the Lord is righteous and has loved righteousness. His face has seen uprightness.
Glory. For the end. Concerning the eighth day. A psalm of David.
Save me, Lord, for the godly are gone, for truthfulness has dwindled among the sons of men.
Everyone speaks empty words to his neighbor. With deceitful lips, with a heart and another heart, they have spoken evil things.
The Lord will destroy all deceitful lips and boastful tongues.
They have said, “We will magnify our tongues. Our lips are our own. Who is lord over us?”
“Because of the suffering of the poor and the groaning of the needy, I will now arise,” says the Lord. “I will place myself in safety and will not hesitate concerning him.”
The words of the Lord are pure words: silver refined by fire, tested in the earth, and purified seven times.
But you, Lord, will preserve us and guard us from this generation forever.
The ungodly walk all around. According to your greatness, you have multiplied the sons of men.
For the end. A psalm of David.
How long, Lord, will you forget me completely? How long will you turn your face away from me?
How long must I take counsel in my soul, with sorrow in my heart day and night? How long will my enemy exalt himself over me?
Look upon me and hear me, Lord my God. Give light to my eyes, lest I fall asleep in death.
Lest my enemy say, “I have prevailed over him.”
Those who afflict me will rejoice if I falter.
But I have trusted in your mercy. My heart will rejoice in your salvation. I will sing to the Lord, who has been good to me, and I will sing praise to the name of the Lord Most High.
For the end. A psalm of David.
The fool has said in his heart, “There is no God.” They have become corrupt and abhorrent in their deeds. There is no one who does good.
The Lord looked down from heaven upon the sons of men to see whether anyone understands or seeks God.
They have all turned aside; together they have become worthless. There is no one who does good, not even one.
Do all those who practice lawlessness not understand, those who devour my people as though eating bread? They have not called upon the Lord.
There they were terrified where there was no reason for fear, for God is among the righteous.
You have put the poor man's counsel to shame, but the Lord is his hope.
Who will bring Israel salvation from Zion? When the Lord brings back his people's captives, Jacob will rejoice and Israel will be glad.
Glory. A Psalm of David.
Lord, who will dwell in your dwelling place? Who will live on your holy mountain?
One who walks without blame, does what is right, and speaks truth in his heart;
who does not deceive with his tongue, does no evil to his neighbor, and does not take up a reproach against those close to him.
The wicked person is despised in his sight, but those who fear the Lord give glory. He swears to his neighbor and does not go back on it.
He does not lend his silver at interest and does not accept bribes against the innocent. Whoever does these things will never be shaken. Body.
A Psalm of David.
Preserve me, Lord, for I have placed my hope in you.
I said to the Lord, “You are my Lord, for you have no need of my good things.”
As for the holy ones who are in his land, the Lord has made all his desires in them wonderful.
Their infirmities multiplied; afterward they hurried. I will not gather their gatherings of blood, nor will I mention their names with my lips.
The Lord is the portion of my inheritance and my cup. You are the one who establishes my inheritance for me.
The measuring lines have fallen for me in splendid places; indeed, my inheritance is splendid to me.
I will bless the Lord who has instructed me; even at night my inward parts have taught me.
That is, the loins. I have always kept the Lord before me, for he is at my right hand so that I will not be shaken.
For this reason my heart will be glad, and my tongue has rejoiced; moreover, my flesh will dwell in hope.
For you will not abandon my soul in Hades, nor will you allow your holy one to see decay.
You have made known to me the paths of life. You will fill me with gladness in your presence. Beauty is at your right hand forever.
For the end. A Prayer of David.
Hear my righteousness, Lord; attend to my prayer. Listen to my plea, which does not come from deceitful lips.
Let my judgment come forth from your presence. My eyes, then, see what is right.
You have tested my heart; you have visited me at night. You have tried me by fire, and no wrongdoing was found in me.
Let my mouth not speak of human deeds. Because of the words of your lips, I have kept to difficult paths.
You have made my steps firm in my paths, so that my feet may not slip.
I have called out because you have heard me, O God. Incline your ear to me and hear my words.
Show your marvelous mercy, you who save those who trust in you from those who oppose your right hand.
Guard me, Lord, like the apple of your eye. You will shelter me under the covering of your wings.
From the presence of the wicked who have terrified me. My enemies have surrounded my soul.
They have shut themselves up in their fat; their mouths have spoken arrogantly.
Those who drive me out have now surrounded me. They have fixed their eyes on bending down toward the ground.
They have seized me like a lion ready for the hunt, and like a young lion dwelling in hiding places.
Rise, Lord, forestall them, [?]. Deliver my soul from the wicked one by your sword, from the enemies of your hand.

Lord, separate them from the few, from the earth, during their lifetime. Their bellies have been filled with your hidden treasures. They have had their fill of sons and have left what remained to their little children.
But I will appear before your face in righteousness. I will be satisfied when your glory appears to me. Glory.

[?] For the end. For the Lord’s servant David, who spoke to the Lord the words of this song on the day when the Lord delivered him from the hands of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul. And he said:
I will love you, Lord, my strength.
The Lord is my stronghold, my refuge, and my deliverer. My God is my helper; I will trust in him. He is my protector, the horn of my salvation, and my defender.
With praise I will call upon the Lord, and I will be saved from my enemies.
The pangs of death surrounded me, and torrents of lawlessness overwhelmed me.
The pangs of Hades surrounded me; the snares of death confronted me. In my distress I called upon the Lord and cried out to my God.
He heard my voice from his holy temple, and my cry before him will enter his ears.
The earth shook and trembled, and the foundations of the mountains were thrown into confusion and shaken, because God was angry with them.
Smoke rose in his anger, and fire will blaze from him. Coals were kindled by him.
He bent the heavens down and descended, and thick darkness was beneath his feet.
He mounted a cherub and flew; he flew on the wings of the wind.
He made darkness his hiding place; his shelter was around him: dark water in the clouds of the air.
At the brightness before him, the clouds passed: hail and burning coals.
The Lord thundered from heaven, and the Most High gave forth his voice.
He sent out arrows and scattered them; he multiplied lightning flashes and threw them into confusion.
The springs of water appeared, and the foundations of the world were uncovered at your rebuke, O Lord, at the blast of the breath of your anger.
He reached down from above and took me; he drew me out of many waters.
He will deliver me from my powerful enemies and from those who hate me, for they grew stronger than I.
They confronted me on the day of my affliction, but the Lord became my support.
He brought me out into a broad place; he delivered me because he delighted in me.
The Lord will repay me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands he will repay me.
For I have kept the ways of the Lord and have not wickedly departed from my God.
For all his judgments are before me, and his ordinances have not departed from me.
I will be blameless with him and keep myself from my lawlessness.
The Lord will repay me according to my righteousness and according to the cleanness of my hands before his eyes.
With the faithful you will be faithful, and with an innocent man you will be innocent.
With the pure you will be pure, and with the crooked you will act crookedly.
For you will save a humble people, O Lord, and you will bring down the eyes of the proud.
For you light my lamp, O Lord; my God, you light up my darkness.
For through you I will be delivered from trouble, and with my God I will climb over a wall.
My God—his way is blameless; the words of the Lord are refined by fire. He is a defender of all who trust in him.
For who is God except the Lord? Or who is God except our God?
God girds me with strength and has made my way blameless.
He makes my feet like a deer's and sets me on high places.
He trains my hands for battle and has made my arms a bronze bow.
You have given me the protection of salvation, and your right hand has supported me. Your discipline has set me completely right, and your discipline itself will teach me.
You have widened the path beneath my steps. My ankles grew weak [?].
I will pursue my enemies and overtake them, and I will not turn back until they are destroyed.
I will crush them, and they will have no strength to stand. They will fall beneath my feet.
You have armed me with strength for battle. You have brought down beneath me all who rise against me.
You have made my enemies turn their backs to me, and you have destroyed those who hate me.
They cried out, but there was no one to save them; they cried to the Lord, but he did not hear them.
I will grind them into dust before the wind; I will wipe them away like mud in the streets.
Deliver me from the disputes of the people. You will make me the head of nations. Foreign people whom I did not know served me.
As soon as they heard, they listened to me. Foreigners lied to me.
Foreigners have grown weak and have limped away from their paths.
The Lord lives, and blessed is my God! May the God of my salvation be exalted!
God gives me vengeance and trains my people under me.
He is my deliverer from my angry enemies. You will raise me above those who rise against me. Deliver me from the unjust man.
Therefore I will praise you among the nations, O Lord, and sing to your name.
He grants great salvation to the king [?] and shows mercy to his Christ, to David and his descendants forever. Anointed one.
GLORY
The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of his hands.
Day pours forth his words to day, and night proclaims knowledge to night.
There are no speeches or words whose voices are not heard [?].
Their proclamation has gone out through all the earth, and their words to the ends of the inhabited world.
He placed his dwelling in the sun. It is like a bridegroom coming out of his bridal chamber; it will rejoice like a mighty man running his course.
It rises from one end of heaven, and its circuit reaches the other end of heaven. There is no one who can hide from its heat.
The law of the Lord is faultless, restoring souls. The testimony of the Lord is trustworthy, making infants wise.
The ordinances of the Lord are right, gladdening hearts. The commandments of the Lord enlighten the eyes from afar.
The fear of the Lord is utterly pure and endures forever. The judgments of the Lord are true and altogether righteous.
They are more desirable than gold and many precious stones, and sweeter than honey and the honeycomb.
For your servant keeps them; in keeping them there is great reward.
Who can understand their own transgressions? Cleanse me from my hidden faults.
And spare your servant from strangers. If they do not rule over me, then I will be blameless and will be cleansed from great sin.
May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart always be pleasing before you, Lord, my helper and my deliverer.
19. For the end. A psalm of David.
May the Lord hear you in the day of trouble. May the name of the God of Jacob protect [?].
May he send you help from the sanctuary and defend you from Zion.
May he remember every sacrifice of yours, and may your burnt offerings be rich.
May the Lord grant you what your heart desires and fulfill your whole plan.
We will rejoice in your salvation and glory in the name of the Lord our God. May the Lord fulfill all your requests.
Now I know that the Lord has saved his anointed. He will hear him from his holy heaven, with the saving power of his right hand.
Some rely on weapons and some on horses, but we will call on the name of [?] the Lord our God.
They stumbled and fell, but we rose and stood upright.
Lord, save the king and hear us on whatever day we call upon you.
20. For the end. A psalm of David.
Lord, the king will be glad in your strength, and we will rejoice greatly in your salvation.
You have given him the desire of your heart, and you have not deprived him of the wish of his lips.
For you met him with blessings [?] of goodness; you placed on his head a crown of precious stone.
He asked you for life, and you gave him length of days forever and ever.
His glory is great through your salvation; they have laid glory and majesty upon him.
For you will give him blessing forever and ever; you will gladden him with joy in your presence.
For the king trusts in the Lord, and through the mercy of the Most High he will not be shaken.
May your hand find all your enemies; may your right hand find all who hate you.
You will make them like a fiery furnace when you appear. The Lord will throw them into confusion in his anger, and fire will devour them.
You will destroy their fruit from the earth and their offspring from among the children of men.
For they directed evil against you; they devised a plan they could not carry out.
For you will make them turn their backs; with what you have in reserve, you will prepare their faces.
Rise up, Lord, in your strength; we will sing and praise your mighty deeds.
Glory. For the end. For the morning help. A psalm of David.
God, my God, attend to me! Why have you forsaken me? The words of my transgressions are far from my salvation.
My God, I cry out by day, and you do not hear, and by night, and this is not folly on my part.
But you dwell in the holy place, the praise of Israel.
Our fathers trusted in you; they trusted, and you delivered them.
They cried out to you and were saved; they trusted in you and were not put to shame.
But I am a worm and not a man, an object of reproach to others and despised by the people.
All who saw me mocked me; they spoke with their mouths and shook their heads.
“He trusted in the Lord; let him deliver him! Let him save him, if he delights in him!”
For you are the one who brought me out of the womb, my hope from my mother's breasts.
I was cast upon you from birth; from my mother's womb you are my God.
Do not depart from me, for trouble is near, and there is no one to help.
Many calves surrounded me; fat young bulls hemmed me in.
They opened their mouths against me like a lion seizing its prey and roaring.
I was poured out like water, and my bones were scattered. My heart became like wax, melting within my body.
My strength dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue stuck to my throat. You brought me down into the dust of death.
For many dogs surrounded me, and a gathering of evildoers besieged me. They nailed down my feet and my hands.
They counted all, all my bones. They dug through [?]. They looked at me and despised me.
They divided my garment among themselves and cast lots for my clothing.
But you, Lord, do not keep your help far from me. Look to my defense.
Deliver my soul from the sword, my only life from the dog's power.
Save me from the mouths of lions, and my humbled self from the horns of unicorns.
I will proclaim your name to my brothers; in the midst of the congregation I will sing your praise.
You who fear the Lord, praise him! All you descendants of Jacob, glorify him! Let all the descendants of Israel fear him.
For he has neither despised nor disdained the prayer of the poor, nor has he turned his face away from me. When I cried out to him, he heard me.
My praise comes from you; in the great congregation I will give thanks to you. I will fulfill my vows before those who fear him.
The poor will eat and be satisfied, and those who seek the Lord will praise him. Hearts will live forever and ever.
All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to the Lord, and all the families of the nations will bow down before him.
For the kingdom belongs to the Lord, and he rules over the nations.
All the prosperous people of the earth ate and bowed down. All who go down into the earth will fall before him, and my soul will live for him.
And my descendants will serve him. The coming generation will proclaim to the Lord.
And they will proclaim his righteousness to people yet to be born, telling what the Lord has done.
Psalm 22. Of David.
The Lord shepherds me, and I will lack nothing.
He settled me in a place of pasture; beside peaceful water he nourished me.
He restored my soul. You have guided me on the path of righteousness.
For his name’s sake, even if I walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me. Your rod and your staff have comforted me.
You have prepared a table before me in the presence of those who trouble me. You have anointed my head with oil. And your cup that makes me drunk—how powerful it is!
And your mercy will pursue me all the days of my life, and may I dwell in the Lord’s house for many days.
Psalm 23. Of David. For the first day of the week.
The earth belongs to the Lord, and everything that fills it, the world and all who live in it.
He has founded it on the seas and established it on the rivers.
Who will ascend the Lord’s mountain, or who will stand in his holy place? One whose hands are innocent and whose heart is pure.
One who has not given his soul over to vanity and has not sworn deceitfully to his neighbor.
He will receive a blessing from the Lord and mercy from God his Savior.
This is the generation of those who seek the Lord, who seek the face of the God of Jacob.
Lift up your gates, you rulers, and be lifted up, you everlasting gates, and the King of glory will enter.
Who is this King of glory? The Lord, strong and mighty, the Lord mighty in battle.
Lift up your gates, you rulers, and be lifted up, you everlasting gates, and the King of glory will enter.
Who is this King of glory? The Lord of hosts: he is the King of glory.
24. Glory. Sessional hymn. A psalm of David.
To you, Lord, I have lifted up my soul.
My God, I have trusted in you; let me never be put to shame, nor let my enemies mock me.
For none who wait for you will be put to shame. Let those who act lawlessly without cause be put to shame.
Make your ways known to me, Lord, and teach me your paths.
Guide me in your truth and teach me, for you are God my Savior, and I have waited for you all day long.
Remember your compassion, Lord, and your mercies, for they have existed from of old.
Do not remember the sins of my youth or my ignorance. Remember me according to your mercy, for the sake of your goodness, Lord.
The Lord is good and upright; therefore he gives sinners a law for their way.
He will guide the meek in judgment; he will teach the meek his ways.
All the Lord’s ways are mercy and truth for those who seek his covenant and his testimonies.
For your name’s sake, Lord, cleanse me of my sin, for it is great.
Who is the person who fears the Lord? He will lay down a law for him in the way he has chosen.
His soul will dwell among good things, and his descendants will inherit the land.
The Lord is the strength of those who fear him, and he will reveal his law to them.
My eyes are always on the Lord, for he will pull my feet out of the snare.
Look upon me and have mercy on me, for I am alone and poor.
The troubles of my heart [?] have multiplied. Bring me out of my distress.
Look upon my humiliation and my toil, and forgive all my sins.
Look at my enemies [?], for they have multiplied, and they have hated me with unjust hatred.
Guard my soul and deliver me; let me not be put to shame, for I have trusted in you.
The innocent and upright have joined themselves to me, because I have waited for you, Lord.
Redeem Israel, O God, from all his troubles.
25. A psalm of David.
Judge me, Lord, for I have walked in my innocence; trusting in the Lord, I will not falter.
Test me, Lord, and examine me; refine my inward parts and my heart.
For your mercy is before my eyes, and I have found favor in your truth.
I have not sat with an assembly of falsehood, and I will not go in with lawbreakers.
I have hated the assembly of evildoers, and I will not sit with the ungodly.
I will wash my hands in innocence and go around your altar, Lord,
so that I may hear the sound of your praise. I will tell of all your wonders.
Lord, I have loved the beauty of your house and the place where your glory dwells.
Do not destroy my soul with the ungodly, or my life with bloodthirsty men,
in whose hands are lawless deeds, whose right hand is filled with bribes.
But I have walked in my innocence. Redeem me, Lord, and have mercy on me.
My foot stands on level ground; in the assemblies I will bless you.
26. Of David, before his anointing.
The Lord is my light and my savior; whom shall I fear? The Lord is the defender of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
When evildoers approach me to devour my flesh, those who oppress me, my enemies, will weaken and fall.
Though an army encamp against me, my heart will not fear. Though war arise against me, I trust in him.
One thing I have asked of the Lord; this I will seek: to dwell in the Lord’s house all the days of my life, to behold the Lord’s beauty and visit his holy temple.
For he hid me in his shelter; in the day of my trouble he concealed me in the secret place of his shelter. You will lift me onto a rock.
And now, behold, he has lifted my head above my enemies. I went around and offered in his shelter a sacrifice of praise and joyful shouting. I sing and will sing praises to the Lord.
Hear, Lord, my voice with which I have cried out. Have mercy on me and hear me.
My heart said to you, “I will seek the Lord.” My face sought you. Your face, Lord, I will seek.
Do not turn your face away from me, and do not turn away in anger from your servant. Be my helper, and do not reject me or abandon me, O God my savior.
For my father and my mother have forsaken me, but the Lord has taken me in.
Lay down your way as a law for me, Lord, and guide me on a straight path.
Because of my enemies, do not hand me over to those who oppress me. For false witnesses have risen against me, whom I did not know, and injustice has lied to itself.
I believe that I will see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living. Wait for the Lord; be courageous, and let your heart grow strong, and wait for the Lord.
Glory. Psalm 27. Of David.
To you, Lord, I will cry. My God, do not remain silent toward me, lest, if you remain silent toward me, I become like those who go down into the pit.
Hear, Lord, the voice of my prayer when I cry to you, when I lift my hands toward your holy temple.
Do not drag me away with sinners, and do not destroy me with those who practice injustice, who speak peace with their neighbors but have evil in their hearts.
Give them, Lord, according to their deeds and according to the evil of their undertakings. Give them according to the works of their hands; repay them what they deserve.
For they have not understood the deeds of the Lord or the works of his hands. You will tear them down and will not build them up.
Blessed is the Lord, for he has heard the voice of my prayer.
The Lord is my helper and my protector. My heart trusted in him, and I was helped. My flesh has blossomed, and I will willingly give thanks to him.
The Lord is the strength of his people, and he is the protector who saves his anointed one.
Save your people, Lord, and bless your inheritance. Shepherd them and lift them up forever.
Psalm 28. Of David. At the departure. Bring to the Lord, sons of God; bring to the Lord young rams; bring to the Lord glory and honor.
Bring to the Lord the glory of his name. Worship the Lord in his holy court.
The voice of the Lord is over the waters. The God of glory has thundered; the Lord is over many waters.
The voice of the Lord is powerful; the voice of the Lord is majestic.
The voice of the Lord shatters cedars, and the Lord will shatter the cedars of Lebanon.
He will crush them like a calf of Lebanon, and the beloved one like a young wild ox.
The voice of the Lord splits the flame of fire.
The voice of the Lord shakes the wilderness, and the Lord will shake the wilderness of Kadesh.
The voice of the Lord makes the deer give birth, and he will lay bare the forests. In his temple everyone speaks of his glory.
The Lord will dwell over the flood, and the Lord sits as king forever. The Lord will give strength to his people. The Lord will bless his people with peace.
For the end. A psalm of a song at the dedication of David’s house.
29. I will exalt you, Lord, because you have lifted me up and have not let my enemies rejoice over me.
Lord my God, I cried out to you, and you healed me.
Lord, you brought my soul up from Hades. You saved me from those who go down into the pit.
Sing to the Lord, his faithful ones; give thanks at the remembrance of his holiness.
For wrath is in his anger, and life is in his favor. Weeping will lodge in the evening, but joy comes in the morning.
But I said in my prosperity, “I will never be shaken.”
Lord, by your favor give strength to my beauty. But you turned your face away, and I was troubled.
To you, Lord, I will cry out, and to my God I will pray.
What profit is there in my blood when I go down into decay? Will the dust give thanks to you? Will it proclaim your truth?
The Lord heard and had mercy on me. The Lord became my helper.
You turned my mourning into joy for me. You tore apart my sackcloth and clothed me with gladness.
So that my glory may sing to you and not be silent. Lord my God, I will give thanks to you forever.
Glory. For the end. A psalm of David, in terror.
30. In you, Lord, I have put my trust; let me never be put to shame. In your righteousness deliver me and rescue me.
Incline your ear to me; hurry to rescue me. Be a protecting God to me and a house of refuge to save me.
For you are my strength and my refuge. For your name’s sake you will guide me and nourish me.
And you will bring me out of the snare [?] which they have hidden for me, for you are my protector, Lord. Into your hands I will commit my spirit. You have redeemed me, Lord, God of truth.
You hated those who heed worthless vanities.
But I have put my trust in the Lord. I will rejoice and be glad in your mercy, for you have looked upon my humiliation. You have saved my soul from troubles.
And you have not shut me up in the hands of enemies. You have set my feet in a spacious place.
Have mercy on me, Lord, for I am in distress. My eye is troubled by anger, as are my soul and my inward parts.
For my life has wasted away in sorrow, and my years in sighing. My strength has failed through poverty, and my bones are troubled.
I became an object of reproach beyond all my enemies, especially to my neighbors, and a terror to those who know me. Those who saw me outside fled from me.
I have been forgotten, like a dead man gone from the heart. I have become like a ruined vessel.
For I heard the abuse of many who lived around me. When they gathered together against me, they plotted to take my life.
But I trusted in you, Lord; I said, “You are my God.”
My fate is in your hands. Deliver me from the hands of my enemies and from those who persecute me.
Make your face shine upon your servant. Save me by your mercy.
Lord, do not let me be put to shame, for I have called upon you. Let the ungodly be put to shame and go down into Hades.
Let deceitful lips fall silent, those that speak lawlessness against the righteous with pride and contempt.
How abundant is your goodness, Lord, which you have stored up for those who fear you, which you have shown to those who trust in you before the children of men!
You will hide them in the secrecy of your presence from human turmoil. You will shelter them under cover from the strife of tongues.
Blessed is the Lord, for he has shown his wondrous mercy in a fortified city.
But I said in my terror, “I have been cast away from the sight of your eyes.” For this reason you heard the voice of my prayer when I cried out to you.
Love the Lord, all his faithful ones, for the Lord seeks truth and repays those who act with excessive pride.
Be courageous, and let your hearts grow strong, all you who trust in the Lord.
Of David. For understanding. 31. Blessed are those whose lawless deeds are [?], whose sins have been covered.
Blessed is the man to whom the Lord does not count sin, and in whose mouth there is no deceit.
For I kept silent, and all my bones wasted away while I cried out all day long.
For day and night your hand lay heavy upon me. I was brought back to suffering when a thorn pierced me.
I acknowledged my lawlessness and did not cover up my sin. I said, “I will confess my lawlessness against myself to the Lord,” and you forgave the ungodliness of my heart.
For this every faithful person will pray to you at a suitable time. Yet even in a flood of many waters, they will not come near him.
You are my refuge from the [?] that surrounds me. My joy, deliver me from those who surround me.
I will give you understanding and guide you along the path you are to take. I will keep my eyes fixed on you.
Do not be like a horse or a mule, which have no understanding. With bit and bridle you must restrain their jaws when they will not come near you.
Many are the blows that fall upon the sinner, but mercy will surround the one who trusts in the Lord.
Be glad in the Lord and rejoice, you righteous, and boast, all you who are upright in heart.
Glory. Sessional hymn. A psalm of David. 32. Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous; praise is fitting for the upright.
Give thanks to the Lord with the lyre; sing to him on a ten-stringed harp.
Sing him a new song; sing well to him with shouts of joy.
For the word of the Lord is right, and all his works are done in faithfulness.
The Lord loves [?] and justice; the earth is full of the Lord’s mercy.
By the word of the Lord the heavens were established, and by the breath of his mouth all their host.
He gathers the waters of the sea as into a wineskin; he stores the depths in storehouses.
Let all the earth fear the Lord; let all who dwell in the world tremble before him.
For he spoke, and they came into being; he commanded, and they were created.
The Lord destroys the counsel of the nations; he rejects the thoughts of the peoples and rejects the plans of rulers.
But the counsel of the Lord remains forever, the thoughts of his heart from generation to generation.
Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord, the people he chose as his own inheritance.
The Lord looked down from heaven; he saw all the children of humankind.
From his prepared dwelling he looked upon all who live on the earth.
He alone formed their hearts; he understands all their deeds.
A king is not saved by a great army, nor is a giant saved by his great strength.
A horse is a false hope for salvation; even by its great strength it will not be saved.
Behold, the eyes of the Lord are upon those who fear him and upon those who hope in his mercy,
to rescue their souls from death and sustain them in famine.
Our soul waits for the Lord, for he is our helper and protector.
For our heart will rejoice in him, and we have put our hope in his holy name.
Let your mercy be upon us, Lord, just as we have put our hope in you.
Psalm 33. Of David, when he changed his appearance before Abimelech, and Abimelech let him go, and he departed.
I will bless the Lord at all times; his praise will always be in my mouth.
My soul will boast in the Lord; let the meek hear and rejoice.
Magnify the Lord with me, and let us exalt his name together.
I sought the Lord, and he heard me, and he will deliver me from all my troubles.
Draw near to him and be enlightened, and your faces will not be put to shame.
This poor man cried out, and the Lord heard him and saved him from all his troubles.
The angel of the Lord will encamp around those who fear him and deliver them.
Taste and see that the Lord is good. Blessed is the man who trusts in him.
Fear the Lord, all his holy ones, for those who fear him lack nothing. Interlude.
The rich became poor and went hungry, but those who seek the Lord will lack no good thing.
Come, children, listen to me; I will teach you the fear of the Lord.
Who is the person who desires life and loves to see good days?
Keep your tongue from evil and your lips from speaking deceit.
Turn away from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it.
The eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and his ears attend to their prayer.
But the face of the Lord is against those who do evil, to wipe out their memory from the earth.
The righteous cried out, and the Lord heard them and delivered them from all their sorrows.
The Lord is near to the brokenhearted, and he will save those who are humble in spirit.
The troubles of the righteous are many, but the Lord will deliver them from them all.
The Lord protects all their bones; not one of them will be broken.
The death of sinners is terrible, and those who hate the righteous will be guilty.
The Lord will redeem the souls of his servants, and none of those who trust in him will be guilty.
34. Glory. A Psalm of David. Judge, O Lord, those who wrong me; fight against those who fight against me.
Take up weapon and shield, and rise to help me.
Draw your weapon and block the way before those who pursue me. Say to my soul, “I am your salvation.”
Let those who seek my life be ashamed and disgraced. Let those who plot evil against me turn back and be put to shame.
Let them be like dust before the wind, with the angel of the Lord driving them on.
Let their way be dark and slippery, with the angel of the Lord pursuing them.
For [?] they hid their deadly net for me; without cause they reviled my soul.
Let a snare he does not know about come upon him, and let the trap he hid catch him; let him fall into that snare.
But my soul will rejoice in the Lord; it will delight in his salvation.
All my bones will say, “Lord, Lord, who is like you? You rescue the poor from the hand of those stronger than they are, and the poor and needy from those who plunder them.”
False witnesses rose up against me; they questioned me about things I knew nothing about.
They repaid me evil for good, leaving my soul bereft.
But when they did vile things to me, they clothed themselves in sackcloth, and I humbled my soul with fasting. And my prayer will return to my own bosom.
I treated him kindly, as a neighbor, as our brother. I humbled myself like someone mourning and grieving.
They rejoiced over me and gathered together. Scourges gathered against me, and I did not know it. They were torn apart and felt no remorse.
They tormented me and taunted me with mockery; they gnashed their teeth at me.
Lord, when will you look upon this? Rescue my soul from their evil deeds, my only life from the lions.
I will give thanks to you, Lord, in the great assembly; among a mighty people I will praise you.
Do not let those who are my enemies unjustly rejoice over me, those who hate me without cause and wink their eyes.
For they spoke peaceably to me, but in their anger they devised deceit.
They opened their mouths wide against me. They said, “Aha, aha! Our eyes have seen it!”
You have seen it, Lord; do not remain silent. Lord, do not withdraw from me.
Rise up, Lord, and attend to my judgment; my God and my Lord, attend to my cause.
Judge me according to your righteousness, Lord my God, and do not let them rejoice over me.
Do not let them say in their hearts, “Aha, just what we wanted!” Do not let them say, “We have swallowed him up!”
Let those who rejoice at my misfortune be ashamed and disgraced together. Let those who boast against me be clothed in shame and disgrace.
Let those who desire my vindication rejoice and be glad, and let those who desire the peace of his servant always say, “May the Lord be magnified!”
And my tongue will meditate on your righteousness and on your praise all day long.
35. For the end. Of David, the servant of the Lord.
[?] the lawbreaker, so that they sin within themselves; for there is no fear of God before his eyes.
For [?] before him, to discover his lawlessness and hate it.
The words of his mouth are lawlessness and deceit. He has refused to understand so that he might do good.
He plotted his lawlessness on his bed. He took his stand on every path that is not good, and he did not reject evil.
Lord, your mercy is in heaven, and your truth reaches to the clouds.
Your righteousness is like the mountains of God; your judgments are a great abyss. You save people and animals, Lord.
How greatly you have multiplied your mercy, O God! The children of men take refuge under the shelter of your wings.
They will drink their fill of the abundance of your house, and you will give them drink from the stream of your delights.
For with you is the fountain of life; in your light we will see light.
Extend your mercy to those who know you, and your righteousness to the upright in heart.
Do not let the foot of the proud come against me, and do not let the hand of a sinner drive me away.
There all who practice lawlessness will fall; they have been cast down and cannot stand.
36. Glory. A psalm of David.
Do not envy those who do evil, nor be jealous of those who practice lawlessness.
For they will quickly wither like grass and soon fall away like green vegetation.
Trust in the Lord and do good; dwell in the land, and you will feed on its riches.
Delight in the Lord, and he will grant you your heart's request.
Lay your way before the Lord; trust in him, and he will act.
He will bring forth your righteousness like the light, and your just cause like the noonday.
Submit to the Lord and entreat him. Do not envy the one who prospers in his [?], the man who breaks the law.
Cease from anger and abandon wrath. Do not be envious, so as to do evil.
For those who do evil will be destroyed, but those who wait for the Lord will possess the land.
In a little while the sinner will be no more; you will seek his place and will not find it.
But the meek will inherit the land and enjoy an abundance of peace.
The sinner watches the righteous man and gnashes his teeth at him.
But the Lord will laugh at him, for he foresees that his day is coming.
The sinners have drawn their swords and bent their bow to shoot down the poor and needy, to slaughter the upright in heart.
Their sword will enter their own hearts, and their bows will be broken.
Better is the little that a righteous man has than the great wealth of sinners.
For the arms of sinners will be broken, but the Lord upholds the righteous.
The Lord knows the way of the blameless, and their inheritance will last forever.
They will not be put to shame in hard times, and in days of famine they will have enough to eat.
For sinners will perish. The Lord’s enemies, just as they are glorified and exalted, will vanish; like smoke they will disappear.
The sinner borrows and does not repay, but the righteous person shows mercy and gives.
For those who bless him will inherit the land, but those who curse him will be destroyed.
A person’s steps are directed by the Lord, and he greatly delights in his way.
When he falls, he will not be shattered, for the Lord supports his hand. [?]
I was young and have grown old, but I have not seen a righteous person abandoned or his descendants begging for bread.
All day long the righteous person shows mercy and lends, and his descendants will be blessed.
Turn away from evil and do good, and live forever and ever.
For the Lord loves justice and will not abandon his righteous ones. They will be preserved forever, but the lawless will be driven out, and the descendants of the ungodly will be destroyed.
But the righteous will inherit the land and live on it forever and ever.
The mouth of the righteous person meditates on wisdom, and his tongue speaks justice.
The law of his God is in his heart, and his steps will not falter.
The sinner watches the righteous person and seeks to kill him.
But the Lord will not leave him in the sinner’s hands or condemn him when he is judged.
Wait for the Lord and keep his way, and he will exalt you to inherit the land. You will see when sinners are destroyed.
I saw an ungodly man exalting himself and towering like the cedars of Lebanon.
He passed away, and behold, he was no more. I searched for him, but his place could not be found.
Preserve innocence and look to uprightness, for a peaceful person will have descendants.
But lawbreakers will be destroyed together, and the descendants of the ungodly will be destroyed.
The salvation of the righteous comes from the Lord, and he is their defender in times of trouble.
The Lord will help them and deliver them. He will rescue them from sinners and save them, because they have trusted in him.
Glory. [?] A Psalm of David, 37. For remembrance concerning the Sabbath.
Lord, do not rebuke me in your fury or discipline me in your anger.
For your arrows have pierced me, and you have laid your hand heavily upon me.
There is no healing for my flesh because of your anger; there is no peace in my bones because of my sins.
For my lawless deeds have risen above my head; like a heavy burden, they weigh upon me.
My wounds stink and fester because of my foolishness.
I have suffered and am utterly bent down; all day long I went about mourning.
For my loins are filled with humiliation, and there is no healing for my flesh.
I was afflicted and brought very low; I roared from the groaning of my heart.
Lord, all my longing lies before you, and my groaning is not hidden from you.
My heart was troubled, my strength left me, and the light of my eyes—it too is no longer with me.
My friends and companions drew near and stood opposite me, while my relatives stood far away.
Those seeking my life used violence, and those seeking my harm spoke empty things and plotted deceit all day long.
But I, like a deaf man, did not hear, and like a mute man, did not open my mouth.
I became like a man who does not hear and has no rebuke in his mouth.
For I have placed my hope in you, Lord; you will hear me, Lord my God.
For I said, “May my enemies never rejoice over me.” When my feet slipped, they boasted against me.
For I am ready for wounds, and my pain is always before me.
For I will declare my lawlessness and be troubled about my sin.
But my enemies live and have grown stronger than I, and those who hate me unjustly have multiplied.
Those who repay me evil for good slandered me because I pursued goodness.
Do not abandon me, Lord. My God, do not withdraw from me. Come to my aid, Lord of my salvation.
For the end. For Jeduthun. A song of David.
I said, “I will guard my ways so that I do not sin with my tongue.”
I set a guard over my mouth when the sinner rose against me.
I became mute and humbled myself, and I refrained from speaking even good things; and my pain was renewed.
My heart grew hot within me, and in my meditation a fire [?]. I spoke with my tongue:
“Lord, tell me my end and what the number of my days is, so that I may understand what I lack.”
See, you have made my days a handbreadth long, and my existence is as nothing before you. Surely every living person is altogether vanity.
Indeed, a person walks about like an image. Yet he troubles himself in vain. Pause. He stores things away and does not know for whom he gathers them.
And now, who is my hope? Is it not the Lord? My existence rests with you.
Deliver me from all my lawless deeds. You have made me an object of reproach to the fool.
I became mute and did not open my mouth, because you did it.
Take your blows away from me, for I have wasted away under the strength of your hand.
With rebukes for lawlessness you have shown a person, and you have made his soul waste away like a spider’s web. Surely every person is vanity. Pause.
Hear my prayer, Lord, and give ear to my plea. Do not remain silent at my tears, for I am a temporary resident with you, a stranger like all my fathers.
Give me relief so that I may rest, before I depart and am no more. [39]
FOR THE END. A PSALM OF DAVID.
I waited patiently for the Lord, and he paid attention to me and heard my prayer.
He brought me up from the pit of [?] and from the muddy mire. He set my feet upon a rock and made my steps firm.
He put a new song into my mouth, a song of praise to our God. Many will see and be afraid, and they will put their trust in the Lord.
Blessed is the man whose hope is the name of the Lord, who has not turned toward vanities and false frenzies.
You have done many wonders, Lord my God, and no one can compare with you in your thoughts. I proclaimed and spoke of them; they increased beyond counting.
You did not desire sacrifice and offering, but you prepared a body for me. You did not ask for burnt offerings for sins.
Then I said, “See, I am coming. In the scroll of the book it is written
about me. I did not desire to do your will, my God, and your law is within my heart.”
I proclaimed the good news of your righteousness in the great congregation. See, I will not restrain my lips; Lord, you know.
I did not hide your righteousness within my heart. I spoke of your truth and your salvation. I did not conceal your mercy and your truth from the great assembly.
But you, Lord, do not withhold your compassion from me. Your mercy and your truth have always protected me.
For evils beyond counting have surrounded me. My lawless deeds have overtaken me, and I could not see. They have become more numerous than the hairs of my head, and my heart has failed me.
Be pleased, Lord, to deliver me. Lord, look to my help.
Let those who seek my life to take it away be put to shame and disgraced together. Let those who wish me harm turn back and be put to shame.
Let those who say to me, “Well done! Well done!” immediately receive their shame.
Let all who seek you rejoice and be glad, Lord. Let those who love your salvation always say, “The Lord be magnified!”
But I am poor and needy; the Lord will care for me. You are my helper and my protector. My God, do not delay.
40. Glory. For the end. A psalm of David.
Blessed is the one who considers the poor and needy. The Lord will deliver him on the day of trouble.
The Lord will protect him and keep him alive, and make him blessed on earth. He will not hand him over to his enemies.
The Lord will help him on his sickbed. You have turned his whole bed about during his illness.
I said, “Lord, have mercy on me. Heal my soul, for I have sinned against you.”
My enemies spoke evil against me: “When will he die and his name perish?”
Someone would come in to see me and speak empty words. His heart gathered lawlessness to itself, and he would go outside and speak.
All my enemies whispered together against me. They plotted evil against me.
They laid a [?] word upon me: “Will the one who lies down not rise again?”
For even the man at peace with me, in whom I trusted, who ate my bread, has greatly increased his treachery against me.
But you, Lord, have mercy on me and raise me up, and I will repay them.
By this I knew that he did not desire me: that my enemy will not rejoice over me.
But you have accepted me because of my innocence, and you have established me before you forever.
Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. So shall it be, so shall it be.
For the end. A psalm of understanding by the sons of Korah. 41.
As a deer longs for springs of water, so my soul longs for you, God.
My soul has thirsted for the mighty and living God. When shall I come and appear before the face of God?
My tears have been my bread day and night, while they said to me every day, “Where is your God?”

I remembered these things and poured out my soul within me: for I will pass through the place of the wondrous shelter to the house of God, with the sound of rejoicing and thanksgiving, the noise of those celebrating a feast.
Why are you sorrowful, my soul, and why do you trouble me? Hope in God, for I will give thanks to him, the salvation of my countenance and my God.
My soul was troubled within me. Therefore I remembered you from the land of the Jordan and Hermon, from the little mountain.
Deep calls to deep at the sound of your floodgates. All your surging waters and your waves will pass over me.
By day the Lord will command his mercy, and by night his song will come from me—a prayer to the God of my life.
I will say to God, “You are my defender. Why have you forgotten me? Why do I go about mourning because of my enemy’s oppression?”
When my bones were being crushed, my enemies taunted me, saying to me every day, “Where is your God?”
Why are you sorrowful, my soul, and why do you trouble me? Hope in God, for I will praise him, the salvation of my countenance and my God.
42. WITHOUT A TITLE. Judge me, O God, and plead my cause. Deliver me from a nation that is not [?], from an unjust and deceitful man.
For you, O God, are my strength. Why have you rejected me, and why do I go about mourning when the enemy oppresses me?
Send out your light and your truth. They have guided me and brought me, and brought me to your holy mountain and to your dwellings.
And I will come to the altar of God, to God, who [?] my youth. I will praise you with the harp, O God, my God.
Why are you deeply sorrowful, my soul, and why do you trouble me? Hope in God, for I will praise him, the salvation of my countenance and my God. Glory.
FOR THE END. AN INSTRUCTION OF THE SONS OF KORAH. A PSALM.
43. O God, we have heard with our ears. Our fathers have told us the work you did in their days, in the days of old.
Your hand destroyed nations, and you planted them. You afflicted peoples and drove them out.
For they did not inherit the land by their own sword, nor did their own arm save them, but your right hand and your arm and the light of your face, because you were pleased with them.
You yourself are my King and my God, who decrees deliverance for Jacob.
Through you we will gore our enemies with horns, and through your name we will bring to nothing those who rise against us.
For I do not trust in my bow, and my sword will not save me.
For you have saved us from those who oppress us, and you have destroyed those who hate us.
In God we will boast all day long, and we will praise your name forever. Pause.
But now you have rejected us and put us to shame, and you do not go out with our armies, O God.
You have made us turn back before our enemies, and those who hate us plundered for themselves.
You have given us up like sheep for food, and you have scattered us among the nations.
You sold your people for no price, and there was no abundance in our shouts.
You have made us a reproach to our neighbors, an object of mockery and ridicule to those around us.
You have made us a byword among the nations, a shaking of the head among the peoples.
All day long my disgrace is before me, and shame covers my face,
because of the voice of the one who insults and slanders, because of the enemy who pursues me.
All these things have come upon us, yet we have not forgotten you or broken your covenant.
Our heart has not turned back, and you have turned our paths away from your way.
For you have humbled us in a place of suffering, and the shadow of death has covered us.
If we have forgotten the name of our God, or stretched out our hands to a [?] god,
will not God search these things out? For he knows the secrets of the heart.
For your sake we are being put to death all day long; they have counted us as sheep for slaughter.
Arise! Why do you sleep, Lord? Awake, and do not reject us forever.
Why do you turn your face away? Why do you forget our poverty and our distress?
For our soul has been brought low into the dust; our belly clings to the ground.
Arise, Lord, help us, and deliver us for your name’s sake.
For the end. Concerning those who are changed. Of the sons of Korah. For understanding. A song about the beloved. 44.
My heart has poured out a good word; I speak of my works to the king. My tongue is the pen of a swift scribe.
You are more beautiful than the sons of men. Grace has been poured upon your lips; therefore God has blessed you forever.
Gird your weapon on your thigh, mighty one,
in your beauty and your splendor. Draw your bow, prosper, and reign, for the sake of truth, gentleness, and righteousness. Your right hand will guide you wondrously.
Your arrows are sharpened, mighty one. Peoples will fall beneath you; your arrows will pierce the hearts of the king’s enemies.
Your throne, O God, is forever and ever; the scepter of your kingdom is a scepter of righteousness.
You have loved righteousness and hated lawlessness; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your companions.
Myrrh, fragrant oil, and cassia come from your garments, from ivory palaces, from which they have made you glad.
Kings’ daughters are among those who honor you. The queen stood at your right hand, clothed in golden garments, richly adorned.
Listen, daughter, and see, and incline your ear. Forget your people and your father’s house.
And the king will desire your beauty, for he is the Lord your God, and you will bow down to him.
And the daughter of Tyre will come with gifts; the rich among the people will seek your favor.
All the glory of the king’s daughter is within; she is clothed in gold fringes, richly embroidered.
Virgins will be brought to the king after her, and her companions will be brought to you.
They will be brought with gladness and joy; they will be brought into the king’s temple.
Your sons have taken the place of your fathers; you will appoint them princes over all the earth.
They will remember your name throughout every generation. Therefore the peoples will give thanks to you forever and ever.
For the end. Concerning the sons of Korah. Concerning hidden things. Psalm 45.
God is our refuge and strength, a helper in the severe troubles that have come upon us.
Therefore we will not be afraid when the earth is shaken and the mountains are moved into the depths of the seas.
Their waters roared and were troubled; the mountains shook at his might.
The river’s streams gladden the city of God; the Most High has made his dwelling holy.
God is in its midst; it will not be shaken. God will help it at the break of dawn.
The nations were thrown into turmoil, and kingdoms tottered. The Most High raised his voice, and the earth shook.
The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our defender.
Come and see the works of God, the wonders he has done on earth.
He puts an end to wars to the ends of the earth. He will shatter the bow and break weapons, and he will burn shields with fire.
Be still and know that I am God. I will be exalted among the nations, and I will be exalted on the earth.
The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our defender. Glory. First.
46. For the end. Concerning the sons of Korah. A psalm.
All you nations, clap your hands; shout to God with a voice of joy.
For the Lord Most High is fearsome, a great king over all the earth.
He subdued peoples under us and nations under our feet.
He chose an inheritance for himself among us, the beauty of Jacob, whom he loved.
God has ascended with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet.
Sing to our God, sing! Sing to our king, sing!
For God is a great king over all the earth. Sing with understanding.
God has become king over all the nations. God sits on his holy throne.
The rulers of the peoples have gathered with the God of Abraham, for the mighty ones of the earth belong to God. He has been greatly exalted.
A psalm of song of the sons of Korah, for the second day of the week. 47.
Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, on his holy mountain.
Firmly rooted, the joy of all the earth, are the mountains of Zion, the slopes of the north, the city of the great King.
God is known in its strongholds when he comes to its defense.
For look, the kings of the earth gathered; they came together.
When they saw it, they were astonished; they were thrown into confusion and shaken.
Trembling seized them there, anguish like that of a woman giving birth.
With a stormy wind he will shatter the ships of Tarshish.
As we have heard, so we have also seen in the city of the Lord of hosts, in the city of our God. God has established it forever. Pause.
We have received your mercy, O God, in the midst of your people.
As your name, O God, so also your praise reaches to the ends of the earth. Your right hand is full of righteousness.
Let Mount Zion rejoice, and let the daughters of Judah be glad.
Because of your judgments, O Lord. Walk around Zion and encircle it; count its towers.
Set your hearts on its strength, and divide up its house.
So that it may be told to another generation: this is our God, our God forever and ever. He will shepherd us forever.
48. For the end. A psalm of the sons of Korah.
Hear this, all nations; give ear, all who live in the world.
Both the earthborn and the sons of men, rich and poor together.
My mouth will speak wisdom, and the meditation of my heart will be understanding.
I will incline my ear to a parable; I will unfold my riddle to the harp.
Why should I fear on an evil day? The lawlessness at my heel will surround me.
Those who trust in their strength and boast of the abundance of their wealth.
A brother will not redeem; will a man redeem? He will not give God a ransom for himself.
And the price of the redemption of his soul.
And he made himself secure forever; he will live to the end.
He will not see destruction when he sees the wise dying. The fool and the senseless person will perish together, and they will leave their wealth to strangers.
Their graves and their houses are forever, their dwellings from generation to generation. They gave their own names to their lands.
And a man, though held in honor, did not [?]; he became like senseless cattle and was like them.
This way of theirs is a stumbling block to them, and afterward they will take pleasure in their own words.

Like sheep they have been placed in Hades; death will shepherd them. The upright will rule over them in the morning, and their help will waste away in Hades. They have been cast down from their glory.
But God will redeem my soul from the power of Hades when he receives me.
Do not be afraid when a man becomes rich, or when the glory of his house increases with him.
For when he dies, will he not leave everything behind? Nor will the glory of his house go down with him.
For his soul will be blessed during his life, and he will praise you when you do good to him.
He will go to the generation of his fathers; he will never see light.
And a man, though held in honor, did not understand; he became like senseless cattle and was like them.
Glory. Psalm 49. A psalm of Asaph. The God of gods, the Lord, has spoken and called the earth from the rising of the sun to its setting.
From Zion comes the splendor of his beauty.
God will come openly. Our God will not remain silent. Fire will blaze before him, and a mighty storm will surround him.
He will call heaven above and the earth to judge his people.
Gather to him his [?], those who establish his covenant through sacrifices.
And the heavens will proclaim his righteousness, for God is judge.
Listen, my people, and I will speak to you. Israel, I will testify against you, for I am God, your God.
I will not rebuke you for your sacrifices; your burnt offerings are always before me.
I will not accept a bull from your house or goats from your flocks.
For all the wild animals of the forest are mine, the cattle on the mountains and the oxen.
I know all the birds of heaven, and the beauty of the fields is with me.
If I become hungry, I will not tell you, for the world and everything that fills it are mine.
Do I eat the flesh of young bulls, or drink the blood of goats?
Offer God a sacrifice of praise, and fulfill your vows to the Most High.
And call upon me on the day of your distress; I will rescue you, and you will glorify me.
But God said to the sinner: Why do you recite my statutes and take my covenant upon your lips?
Yet you hated instruction and cast my words behind you.
When you saw a thief, you ran with him, and you joined your lot with adulterers.
Your mouth multiplied evil, and your tongue wove deceit.
You sat and slandered your brother, and laid a stumbling block for your mother's son.
You did these things, and I kept silent. You wickedly supposed that I would be like you. I will rebuke you and set your sins before your face.
Understand these things, you who forget God, lest he seize you and there be no one to rescue you.
A sacrifice of praise will glorify me, and there is the way by which I will show him my salvation.
FOR THE END. A PSALM OF DAVID.
WHEN NATHAN THE PROPHET CAME TO HIM, AFTER HE HAD GONE IN TO BATHSHEBA. 50.
Have mercy on me, O God, according to your great mercy, and according to your abundant compassion blot out my transgressions.
Wash me thoroughly from my lawlessness, and cleanse me from my sin.
For I know my lawlessness, and my sin is always before me.
Against you alone have I sinned, and I have done evil before you, so that you may be justified in your words and prevail when you are judged.
For behold, I was conceived in lawlessness, and in sins my mother bore me.
For behold, you have loved truth; you have revealed to me your unknown and hidden wisdom.
You will sprinkle me with hyssop, and I will be cleansed; you will wash me, and I will become whiter than snow.
You will let me hear joy and gladness; the bones that have been humbled will rejoice.
Turn your face away from my sins, and blot out all my transgressions.
Create a clean heart in me, O God, and renew an upright spirit within me.
Do not cast me away from your presence, and do not take your Holy Spirit from me.
Restore to me the joy of your salvation, and strengthen me with a governing spirit.
I will teach the lawless your ways, and the ungodly will return to you.
Deliver me from bloodshed, O God, God of my salvation, and my tongue will rejoice in your righteousness.
Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will proclaim your praise.
For if you had desired a sacrifice, I would have given it; but you take no pleasure in whole burnt offerings.
The sacrifice to God is a broken spirit. God will not despise a broken and humbled heart.
Lord, do good to Zion in your favor, and let the walls of Jerusalem be built.
Then you will take pleasure in a righteous sacrifice, offerings and whole burnt offerings. Then they will lay calves upon your altar.
Glory. For the end. An instruction of David, when Doeg the Edomite came and reported to Saul
and said to him, “David has come into Abimelech’s house.” 51.
Why do you boast of evil, mighty man? Lawlessness
all day long. Your tongue has devised injustice; like a sharpened razor, you have practiced deceit.
You have loved evil more than goodness, injustice rather than speaking righteousness.
You have loved every destructive word, deceitful tongue.
Therefore God will destroy you completely. He will tear you out and remove you from your dwelling, and uproot you from the land of the living. Pause.
The righteous will see and be afraid. They will laugh at him and say:
“Here is the man who did not make God his helper, but trusted in his great wealth and grew strong in his own vanity.”
But I am like a fruitful olive tree in the house of God. I trust in God’s mercy forever and ever.
I will give thanks to you forever, because you have acted. And I will wait for your name, for it is good before your [?].
For the end. Concerning Mahalath. An instruction of David. 52.
The fool has said in his heart, “There is no God.” They have become corrupt and abominable in their lawlessness; there is no one who does good.
God looked down from [?] upon the children of humankind, to see whether there was anyone who understood or sought God.
They have all turned aside; together they have become useless. There is no one who does good, not even one.
Will all those who practice lawlessness never understand? They devour my people as if they were bread, and have not called upon God.
There they were afraid where there was nothing to fear, because God scattered the [?] of the one who pleases people. They were put to shame, because God rejected them.
Who will bring Israel’s salvation from Zion? When God brings his people back from captivity, Jacob will rejoice and Israel will be glad.
For the end, with songs. A meditation by David.
When the Ziphites came and said to Saul, “Is not David hiding among us?”
O God, save me by your name, and judge my cause by your might.
O God, hear my prayer; give ear to the words of my mouth.
For strangers have risen against me, and mighty men have sought my life. They have not set God before them. Interlude.
Look, God helps me, and the Lord is the defender of my life.
Return evil to my enemies; destroy them in your faithfulness.
I will sacrifice to you willingly; I will praise your name, Lord, for it is good.
For you have delivered me from every trouble, and my eye has looked upon my enemies.
For the end, with songs. A meditation by David. A psalm.
Give ear to my prayer, O God, and do not disregard my plea.
Attend to me and hear me. I was distressed in my sorrow and troubled.
Because of the enemy’s voice and the sinner’s oppression, for they brought lawlessness upon me and opposed me in anger.
My heart was troubled within me, and the fear of death fell upon me.
Fear and trembling came upon me, and darkness covered me.
And I said, “Who will give me wings like a dove’s? Then I will fly away and rest.”
See, I fled far away and settled in the wilderness. Interlude.
I waited for God to save me from faintness of spirit and from the storm.
Drown them, Lord, and divide their tongues, for I have seen lawlessness and strife in the city.
Day and night it goes around you [?] along its walls; lawlessness, hardship, and injustice are within it.
Usury and deceit have not ceased in its streets.
For if an enemy had insulted me, I would have borne it; and if someone who hated me had spoken arrogantly against me, I would have hidden from him.
But you, a man of one mind with me, my master and my acquaintance—
You who [?] food for me; we walked in the house of God with [?] purpose.
Let death come upon them; let them go down alive into Hades, for evil is in their dwellings, in their midst.
I cried out to God, and the Lord heard me.
Evening, morning, and noon I will speak; I will declare that he has heard my voice.
He will deliver my soul in peace from those who draw near to me, for there were many with me.
God will hear and humble them, he who exists before the ages. For there is no change in them, because they have not feared God.
He will stretch out his hand in retribution. They have defiled his covenant on earth.
They were divided by the anger of his face, and their hearts drew near. Their words became softer than oil, yet they are arrows.
Cast your care upon the Lord, and he will sustain you. He will never allow the righteous to be shaken.
But you, O God, will bring them down into the pit of destruction. Bloodthirsty and deceitful men will not live out half their days. But I, O Lord, trust in you. Glory.
For the end. Concerning the people far removed [?] from the holy things. For David, as an inscription on a pillar, when the foreigners seized him in Egypt. 55.
Have mercy on me, O God, for a man has trampled me down. All day long he has fought against me and oppressed me.
My enemies have trampled me down all day long, for many fight against me from on high.
All day long I will not be afraid, but I will trust in you.
In God I will praise my words. In God I have put my trust; I will not fear what flesh can do to me.
