All day long my words were hateful to them. All their thoughts against me are for evil.
They will settle together and hide. They will watch my steps, just as they have waited for my soul. You will save them for nothing.
In anger you will strike down the peoples.
O God, I have told you of my life. You have placed my tears before you, according to your promise.
My enemies will turn back on the day when I call upon you. This I have known: you are my God.
In God I will praise the utterance; in the Lord I will praise the word.
Trusting in God, I will not fear what a man can do to me.
Vows are within me, O God, which I will fulfill in praise of you.
For you have delivered my soul from death, my eyes from tears, and my feet from stumbling. I will be pleasing before the Lord in the land of the living.
For the end. Destroy. Of David, an inscription on a pillar, when he fled from Saul into the cave. 56.
Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me, for my soul has trusted in you. In the shadow of your wings I will take refuge until lawlessness has passed.
I will cry out to God Most High, to God who has done good to me. Pause.
He sent from heaven and saved me; he will put those who trample me to shame. God sent his mercy and his truth.
And he delivered my soul. I lay down troubled among young lions. The sons of men—their teeth are weapons and arrows, and their tongue is a sharp sword.
Be exalted above the heavens, O God, and let your glory be over all the earth.
They prepared a net for my feet and bowed down my soul. They dug a pit before me and fell into it themselves.
My heart is ready, O God; my heart is ready. I sing and will sing praises to my glory.
Awake, my glory! Awake, harp and lyre!
I will rise early and give thanks to you among the peoples, Lord. I will sing praises to you among the nations.
For your mercy has grown great as far as the heavens, and your truth as far as the clouds.
Be exalted above the heavens, O God, and let your glory be over all the earth.
For the end. Do not destroy. Of David. An inscription [?]. 57.
If you truly speak what is right, judge rightly, sons of men.
For in your hearts you commit lawlessness on earth; your hands weave injustice.
Sinners have been estranged from the womb; they went astray from birth, speaking lies.
Their fury is like that of a serpent, like a deaf asp that stops its ears,
which will not hear the voice of a charmer, though charmed by a skilled enchanter.
God will shatter their teeth in their mouths. The Lord has shattered the lions’ molars.
They will come to nothing like water flowing away. He will draw his bow until they grow weak.
Like melted wax they will be swept away. Fire fell upon them, and they did not see the sun.
Before your thorns recognize the buckthorn, he will devour you alive, as in wrath.
The righteous man will rejoice when he sees vengeance; he will wash his hands in the sinner’s blood.
And a man will say, “There is indeed fruit for the righteous; there is indeed a God who judges them on earth.”
Glory. For the end. Do not destroy. Of David. An inscription, when Saul sent men and had his house watched in order to kill him. 58.
Rescue me from my enemies, O God, and deliver me from those who rise against me.
Deliver me from those who practice lawlessness, and save me from bloodthirsty men.
For look, they have hunted down my soul; mighty men have attacked me—not for my lawlessness or my sin, Lord.
Without wrongdoing I ran and went straight ahead. Rise to meet me, and see.
And you, Lord God of hosts, God of Israel, attend to the punishment of all the nations. Have no mercy on any who practice lawlessness.
They will return in the evening and howl like a dog, and go around the city.
Look, they answer with their mouths, and weapons are on their lips, for who hears?
But you, Lord, will laugh at them; you will bring all the nations to nothing.
I will keep my strength for you, for you, God, are my defender.
My God—his mercy will come to meet me. My God will let me look upon my enemies.
Do not kill them, lest they ever forget your law. Scatter them by your power and bring them down, Lord, my protector.
The sin of their mouths is the word of their lips. They will be caught in their own pride, and because of their cursing and lies they will be exposed at their end.
In consuming wrath they will be no more. And they will know that God rules over Jacob and the ends of the earth.
They will return in the evening and howl like a dog, and go around the city.
They will wander about to eat, and if they are not satisfied, they will grumble.
But I will sing through your strength, and they will rejoice in the morning in your mercy, for he became my defender and my refuge on the day of my distress.
You are my helper; I will sing to you, for you, God, are my defender, my God, my mercy.
For the end. Concerning those who will be changed. For an inscription. Of David.
For instruction. When he burned Syrian Mesopotamia and Syria of Zobah, and Joab returned and struck down twelve thousand in the Valley of Salt. 59.
My God, you have rejected us and broken us down. You have been angry and have had mercy on us.
You shook the earth and threw it into turmoil. Heal its fractures, for it is shaking.
You showed your people harsh things. You made us drink the wine of bewilderment.
You gave those who fear you a banner, so that they might flee from the bow. Selah.
So that your beloved may be delivered, save with your right hand, with your right hand, and hear me.
God has spoken in his holy place: I will rejoice and divide Shechem, and measure out the valley of settlements.
Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine, and Ephraim is the strength of my head.
Judah is my king. Moab is the basin of my hope. Over Edom I will stretch out my sandal. Foreigners have submitted to me.
Who will lead me into the fortified city? Or who will guide me as far as Edom?
Was it not you, O God, who rejected us? And will you not go out, O God, with our armies?
Give us help in distress, for human help is worthless.
With God we will act mightily, and he will bring to nothing those who oppress us.
60. For the end. Among the hymns. Of David.
Hear my prayer, O God.
Listen to my plea. From the ends of the earth I cried to you. When my heart grew faint, you lifted me onto a rock.
You have guided me, for you have been my hope, a strong tower against the enemy.
I will dwell in your tent forever. I will take shelter beneath the covering of your wings. Selah.
For you, O God, have heard my prayers. You have given an inheritance to those who fear your name.
You will add days to the king’s days; his years will extend through generation after generation.
He will remain forever before God. Who will seek out his mercy and truth?
So I will sing to your name forever, fulfilling my vows day by day.
Glory. 61. For the end. For Jeduthun. A psalm of David.
Will not my soul submit to God? For my salvation comes from him.
For he is my God and my Savior, my protector; I will not be greatly shaken.
How long will you attack a man, all of you trying to kill him, as though he were a leaning wall and a tottering fence?
Yet they plotted to cast down my honor; they ran in thirst. With their mouths they blessed him. Selah. But in their hearts they uttered curses.
Yet submit to God, my soul, for my patient hope comes from him.
For he is my God and my Savior, my protector; I will not be moved.
My salvation and my glory rest in God. My God is my help, and my hope is in God.
Trust in him, all you assembled people. Pour out your hearts before him, for God is our protector. Selah.
The sons of men are only emptiness; the sons of men are false. On the scales they do not prove true.
Together they come from emptiness. Do not trust in wrongdoing or desire plunder. If wealth flows past you, do not set your heart on it.
God spoke once; I heard these two things:
That power belongs to God, and mercy belongs to you, O Lord, for you repay each person according to their deeds.
A psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Edom. 62.
O God, my God, I seek you at dawn. My soul has thirsted for you. How often my flesh has longed for you, in a desert land, impassable and without water.
Thus I appeared before you in the sanctuary, to see your power and your glory.
For your mercy is better than life. My lips will praise you.
So I will bless you throughout my life, and in your name I will lift up my hands.
May my soul be filled as with fat and rich food, and my mouth will praise you with joyful lips.
When I remembered you on my bed, I meditated on you at dawn.
For you have been my helper, and in the shelter of your wings I will rejoice.
My soul has clung to you, and your right hand has upheld me.
But they sought my life in vain. Let them go down into the depths of the earth.
They will be delivered into the power of the sword; they will become portions for foxes.
But the king will rejoice in God. Everyone who swears by him will boast, for the mouths of those who speak falsehood have been stopped.
For the end. A psalm of David. 63.
Hear my voice, O God, when I pray to you. Deliver my soul from fear of the enemy.
Shelter me from the gathering of the wicked and from the multitude of those who do wrong.
They sharpened their tongues like a sword. They bent their bow, and a bitter word,
to shoot at the blameless person in secret. Suddenly they will shoot at him and will not be afraid.
They made their wicked plan firm among themselves. They spoke of hiding snares. They said, “Who will see them?”
They searched out lawlessness; those making searches grew weary. A person will draw near, and the heart is deep.
And God will be exalted. Their wounds became the arrows of little children.
Their tongues grew weak within them. All who saw them were troubled.
And every person was afraid. They proclaimed the works of God and understood what he had done.
The righteous person will rejoice in the Lord and put his trust in him, and all the upright in heart will boast.
Glory. Kathisma. For the end. A psalm of David. A song of Jeremiah and Ezekiel, for the people in exile, when they were about to depart. 64.
A song is fitting for you, O God, in Zion, and a vow will be fulfilled to you in Jerusalem.
Hear my prayer. All flesh will come to you.
The words of lawless people overpower us, but you will cleanse away our ungodliness.
Blessed is the one whom you have chosen and accepted; he will dwell in your courts. We will be filled with the good things of your house.
Your holy temple is wondrous in righteousness. Hear us, O God our Savior, the hope of all the ends of the earth and of those far away at sea.
You establish the mountains by your strength, girded with power.
You stir up the depths of the sea. Who can withstand the roar of its waves?
The nations will be thrown into turmoil, and those who live at the ends of the earth will fear your signs. You will adorn the coming of morning and evening.
You have visited the earth and given it drink; you have greatly enriched it. The river of God has filled with water. You have prepared food for them, for such is your preparation.
Water its furrows; multiply its [?]. The sower will rejoice in its drops.
You will bless the crown of the year of your goodness, and your fields will be filled with abundance.
The beautiful places of the wilderness will grow rich, and the hills will gird themselves with joy.
The rams of the flock have clothed themselves, and the valleys will abound in wheat. They will cry out and sing.
65. For the end. A psalm, a song about the resurrection. Of David. Anonymous.
Shout to the Lord, all the earth. Sing to his name; give him glory and praise.
Say to God, “How fearsome are your deeds! Because of your great power, your enemies will deal falsely with you.”
Let all the earth bow down and sing to you. Let them sing to your name, O Most High. Interlude.
Come and see the works of God. How fearsome he is, beyond the sons of men, turning the sea into dry land.
They will pass through the river on foot. There we will rejoice in him,
who rules by his power forever. His eyes watch over the nations. Let those who provoke him exalt themselves. Interlude.
Bless our God, you nations, and make the sound of his praise heard.
He has kept my soul alive and has not let my feet be shaken.
For you have tested us, O God; you have refined us as silver is refined.
You brought us into a net; you laid affliction upon our backs.
You set people over our heads. We passed through fire and water, and you brought us out into rest.
I will enter your house with burnt offerings; I will fulfill my vows to you.
Which my lips uttered and my mouth spoke in my distress.
I will offer you burnt offerings full of marrow, with the incense of rams. I will offer you oxen and goats. Selah.
Come, listen, and I will tell you, all you who fear God, everything he has done for my soul.
I cried out to him with my mouth, and exalted him beneath my tongue.
If I had regarded unrighteousness in my heart, the Lord would not have heard me.
For this reason God heard me; he attended to the voice of my prayer.
Blessed is God, who will not reject my prayer or withdraw his mercy from me.
For the end. A song among songs. A psalm without an inscription. 66.
O God, have compassion on us and bless us; make your face shine upon us and have mercy on us. Selah.
So that we may know your way on earth, your salvation among all nations.
Let the peoples praise you, O God; let all the peoples praise you.
Let the nations be glad and rejoice, for you judge the peoples rightly. Selah. And you will guide the nations on earth. Psalm.
Let the peoples praise you, O God; let all the peoples praise you.
The earth will yield its fruit. Bless us, O God.
Our God, bless us, O God, and all the ends of the earth will fear you.
Glory. 67. For the end. A song. A psalm of David.
God will arise, and his enemies will scatter, and all who hate him will flee from his presence.
As smoke vanishes, so they will vanish; as wax melts before fire, so sinners will perish before God, and the righteous will be glad. Selah.
And they will rejoice before God and delight in his gladness.
Sing to God; sing praises to his name. Prepare a way for him who has ascended into the west. The Lord is his name; rejoice before him.
They will be troubled before him, the father of orphans and judge of widows. God is in his holy place.
God settles those of differing minds in a house, bringing out those bound in chains with might; likewise those who provoke him, who dwell in tombs.
O God, when you went out before your people—the earth [?]—when you passed through the wilderness,
The earth shook, and the heavens dripped before the God of Sinai, before the God of Israel. Selah.
You will set aside rain freely given, O God, for your inheritance. It grew weak, but you restored it.
Your living creatures dwelt in it. In your goodness, O God, you provided for the poor.
The Lord will give a word to those who proclaim good news with great power.
The king of the powers of the beloved will divide the spoils for the beauty of the house.
Even if you sleep between the boundaries, the wings of a dove are silvered, and its back gleams with gold. Interlude.
When the Heavenly One scatters kings upon it, they will become white as snow on Zalmon.
The mountain of God is a rich mountain, a rugged mountain, a rich mountain.
Why do you look with suspicion at the rugged mountain? This is the mountain where God was pleased to dwell. Indeed, the Lord will dwell there forever.
God’s chariots are tens of thousands upon tens of thousands, thousands in abundance. The Lord is among them, at Sinai, in the holy place.
You ascended on high; you took captives. You received gifts among people. For even those who resist [?].
Glory. Psalm 8. For the end. Concerning those who have changed. Of David. 68.
Save me, O God, for the waters have reached my soul.
I have sunk into deep mire, and there is no firm footing. I have come into the depths of the sea, and a storm has overwhelmed me.
I have grown weary from crying out; my throat has fallen silent. My eyes have failed as I wait for my God.
Those who hate me without cause have become more numerous than the hairs of my head. My enemies who persecute me unjustly have grown strong. Then I repaid what I had not stolen.
O God, you know my foolishness, and my sins have not been hidden from you.
Do not let those who wait for you be put to shame because of me, O Lord, Lord of hosts. Do not let those who seek you be disgraced because of me, O God of Israel.
For your sake I have borne reproach; shame has covered my face.
I have become a stranger to my brothers, a foreigner to my mother’s sons.
For zeal for your house will consume me, and the reproaches of those who reproach you have fallen upon me.
I covered my soul with fasting, and it became a reproach to me.
I made sackcloth my clothing, and I became a byword to them.
Those who sat at the gates mocked me, and those who drank wine sang about me.
But I turn to you with my prayer, O Lord, at a time of favor, O God. In the abundance of your mercy, answer me with the faithfulness of your salvation.
Save me from the mire, so that I do not sink. Deliver me from those who hate me and from the deep waters.
Do not let the floodwaters overwhelm me, or the deep swallow me, or the pit close its mouth over me.
Hear me, Lord, for your mercy is good; look upon me according to the abundance of your compassion.
Do not turn your face away from your servant. Because I am in distress, hear me quickly.
Attend to my soul and rescue it; deliver me because of my enemies.
For you know my disgrace, my shame, and my dishonor. All who torment me are before you.
My soul expected disgrace and suffering. I waited for someone to grieve with me, but there was no one, and for someone to comfort me, but I found none.
They gave me gall for food, and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
Let the table before them become a snare, a retribution, and a stumbling block.
Let their eyes be darkened so that they cannot see, and bend their backs down completely.
Pour out your anger upon them, and let your furious wrath seize them.
Let their dwelling be deserted, and let no one live in their tents.
For they persecuted the one you struck, and they added to the pain of my wounds.
They added lawlessness to their lawlessness. Let them not enter into your righteousness.
Let them be erased from the books of the living, and let them not be recorded with the righteous.
I am poor and suffering; your salvation, O God, has taken me in.
I will praise the name of my God with a song; I will magnify him with praise.
This will please God more than a young bull growing horns and hooves.
Let the poor see and rejoice. Seek God, and your soul will live.
For the Lord has heard the poor, and he will not despise his prisoners.
Let heaven and earth praise him, the sea and everything that moves in it.
For God will save Zion, and the cities of Judah will be rebuilt. They will settle there and inherit it.
The descendants of your servants will possess it, and those who love your name will dwell in it.
69. For the end. For David. A remembrance, because the Lord saved me.
O God, attend to my help. Lord, hurry to help me.
Let those who seek my life be put to shame and disgraced. Let those who wish me harm turn back and be put to shame.
Let those who say to me, “Well done! Well done!” turn back at once in shame.
Let all who seek you rejoice and be glad in you, Lord. Let those who love your salvation always say, “May the Lord be magnified!”
But I am poor and needy; God, help me. You are my helper and my deliverer; Lord, do not delay.
Glory. [?] A psalm of David, for the sons of Jonadab and those taken captive earlier.
In you, Lord, I have placed my hope; let me be put to shame forever.
Deliver me in your righteousness. Turn your ear toward me and save me.
Be to me a protecting God and a strong place to save me, for you are my stronghold and my refuge.
My God, deliver me from the hand of the sinner, from the hand of the lawbreaker and the oppressor.
For you are my patient endurance, Lord; the Lord is my hope from my youth.
On you I have relied from the womb and from my mother’s belly. You are my protector. My song is always of you.
I have become a wonder to many, and you are my mighty helper.
Let my mouth be filled with praise, so that I may sing of your glory and your majesty all day long.
Do not cast me away in old age; when my strength fails, do not abandon me.
For my enemies have spoken against me, and those who lie in wait for my life have conspired together,
saying, “God has abandoned him. Pursue him and seize him, for there is no one to deliver him.”
My God, do not go far from me; my God, attend to my help.
Let those who slander my soul be put to shame and perish. Let those who seek to harm me be clothed in shame and disgrace.
But I always hope in you, and I will add to all your praise.
My mouth will proclaim your righteousness and your salvation all day long, for I have not known a scribe.
I will enter in the Lord’s strength. Lord, I will remember your righteousness, yours alone.
My God, since you have taught me from my youth, even to this day I will proclaim your wonders.
Even into old age [?], my God, do not abandon me, until I proclaim your arm to this coming generation.
By your power and your righteousness, O God of the heights, who have done great things! God, who is like you?
How many grievous troubles you have shown me! Yet you have turned back and given me life, and long ago you brought me up from the depths of the earth.
You have increased your greatness upon me, and you have turned back and comforted me, and you have brought me up again from the depths of the earth.
For I will praise you among the peoples, Lord, and your truth with instruments of psalmody, O God. I will sing to you on the lyre, O Holy One of Israel.
My lips will rejoice when I sing to you, and so will my soul, which you have redeemed.
My tongue too will meditate on your righteousness all day long, when those who seek to harm me are put to shame and disgraced.
71. For the end. A psalm of David, concerning Solomon.
O God, give your judgment to the king, and your righteousness to the king’s son,
to judge your people with righteousness and your poor with justice.
Let the mountains receive peace for the people, and the hills righteousness.
He will judge the poor among the people, save the children of the needy, and humble the slanderer.
He will endure with the sun, and before the moon, from generation to generation.
He will come down like rain upon a fleece, and like drops falling upon the earth.
In his days righteousness will spring up, and abundant peace, until the moon is taken away.
He will rule from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the inhabited world.
Before him Ethiopians, Moors, will fall down, and his enemies will lick the dust.
The kings of Tarshish [?] will bring gifts; the kings of Arabia and Sheba will bring gifts.
The kings of the earth will bow down to him; all nations will serve him.
For he has delivered the poor from the powerful, and the needy man who had a helper.
He will spare the poor and needy, and save the souls of the needy.
He will deliver their souls from usury and injustice, and his name will be honored among them.
He will live, and gold from Arabia will be given to him. They will pray to him continually; he will bless him all day long.
There will be firm support on the earth, on the mountaintops. [?] His fruit will rise higher than Lebanon, and people will flourish from the city like the grass of the earth.
May his name be blessed forever. 12. His name endures before the sun. All the tribes of the earth will be blessed in him; all nations will call him blessed.
Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, who alone does wonders.
And blessed is his glorious name forever and ever. The whole earth will be filled with his glory. So be it, so be it. Glory.
72. The many songs of David, the son of Jesse, have ended. A psalm of Asaph.
How good the God of Israel is to those who are upright in heart!
But my feet had almost slipped; my steps had nearly slid away.
For I envied the lawless when I saw the peace of sinners.
For there is no struggle in their death, and no firmness in their wounds.
They do not share in human toil, and they will not suffer wounds with other people.
Therefore pride held them fast to the end. They clothed themselves in their injustice and ungodliness.
Their injustice will come forth as though from fatness; they will go beyond their hearts’ desires.
They plotted and spoke maliciously; they spoke injustice from on high.
They set their mouths against heaven, and their tongue ranged over the earth.
Therefore my people will return here, and a full day will be found among them.
And they said, “How does God know? And is there knowledge in the Most High?”
Look, these are the sinners, prospering; they have held on to wealth forever.
And I said, “Surely I have made my heart righteous in vain, and washed my hands in innocence.”
And I was beaten all day long, and my accuser was there at dawn.
If I said, “I will speak this way,” behold, I put to the test the generation of your sons, to which I had pledged myself.
And I thought about understanding this. It is a hardship before me,
until I enter God’s sanctuary and understand their final end.
Yet because of their deceit you have appointed evils for them; you cast them down when they grew proud.
How suddenly they became desolate! They came to an end; they perished because of their lawlessness.
Like the dream of someone waking, Lord, in your city they despised their image.
For my heart grew hot, and my inward parts [?].
And I was brought low and did not understand; I was like a beast before you.
Yet I am always with you. You held my right hand,
and guided me by your counsel, and received me with glory.
For what do I have in heaven? And apart from you, what have I desired on earth?
My heart and my flesh have failed. God is the God of my heart, and God is my portion forever.
For behold, those who distance themselves from you will perish. You have destroyed everyone who is unfaithful to you.
But it is good for me to draw near to God, to place my hope in the Lord, so that I may proclaim all your praises at the gates of the daughter of Zion.
73. An instruction of Asaph.
Why, O God, have you rejected us forever? Why has your anger raged against the sheep of your pasture?
Remember your congregation, which you acquired from the beginning. You redeemed the rod of your inheritance—this Mount Zion, where you made your dwelling.
Lift up your hands against their arrogance once and for all, against all the evil the enemy has done in your sanctuary.
Those who hate you boasted in the midst of your festival. They set up their signs as signs, and did not understand.
As at the exit above, as in a grove of trees, they hacked apart its doors with axes.
Together they demolished it with axe and pick.
They set fire to your sanctuary; they desecrated the dwelling place of your name, bringing it to the ground.
Their kinsmen said together in their hearts, “Come, let us put an end to all God's festivals on the earth.”
We have not seen our signs. There is no longer a prophet [?], and he will no longer know us.
How long, O Lord, will the enemy taunt you? Will the adversary provoke your name forever?
Why do you draw back your hand, and your right hand from within your bosom, forever?
But God is our King from before the ages; he has brought about salvation in the midst of the earth.
You made the sea firm by your power; you crushed the heads of the serpents in the water.
You shattered the serpent's head; you gave it as food to the Ethiopian people. MOORS.
You split open springs and streams; you dried up flooded rivers.
The day is yours, and the night is yours; you established the dawn and the sun.
You made all the boundaries of the earth; you created summer and spring. Remember this.
The enemy has taunted the Lord, and a foolish people have provoked your name.
Do not hand over to wild beasts the soul that praises you. Do not forget the souls of your poor forever.
Look upon your covenant, for the dark places of the earth are filled with homes of wrongdoing.
Let no one turn back humbled and ashamed. The needy and the poor will praise your name.
Arise, O God, plead your cause. Remember the insults directed at you by the fool all day long.
Do not forget the voice of those who pray to you. The arrogance of those who hate you rises continually. GLORY.
74. For the end. Do not destroy. Of Asaph. A psalm, a song.
I will give thanks to you, O God; I will give thanks and call upon your name. I will tell of all your wonders.
When I receive the appointed time, I will judge rightly.
The earth melted away, and all who live on it. I established its pillars.
I said to the lawbreakers, “Do not break the law,” and to those who sin, “Do not lift up your horn.
Do not raise your horn on high, and [?] speak unrighteous things against God.”
For neither from the east nor from the west, nor from the wilderness mountains,
for God is the judge. He humbles one and raises another.
For in the Lord’s hand is a cup of unmixed wine, full of mixture. He poured from this one into that one. Yet its dregs were not hidden; all the sinners of the earth will drink them.
But I will rejoice forever; I will sing to the God of Jacob. I will break all the horns of sinners, and the horn of the righteous will be raised.
75. For the end. With songs. A psalm of Asaph. A song concerning the Assyrian.
God is known in Judea; his name is great in Israel.
His place came to be in peace, and his dwelling in Zion.
There he shattered the strength of bows, the shield, and choice weapons.
You shine wonderfully from the everlasting mountains.
All the foolish in heart were troubled. They slept their sleep, and all the men of wealth found nothing with their hands.
At your rebuke, O God of Jacob, those mounted on horses fell asleep.
You are fearsome, and who can withstand you? From that time comes your wrath.
He made judgment heard from heaven. The earth was afraid and fell silent,
when God rises for judgment, to save all the meek of the earth. Musical interlude.
For human thought will give thanks to you, and the remainder of thought will keep a feast for you.
Make vows and fulfill them to the Lord our God. All who surround him will bring gifts
to the fearsome one, who takes away the spirits of princes, who is more fearsome than the kings of the earth.
76. For the end. Concerning Jeduthun. A psalm of Asaph.
With my voice I cried to the Lord, with my voice to God, and he listened to me.
In the day of my distress I sought God. With my hands I sought comfort before him at night, and I was not deceived. My soul refused to be comforted.
I remembered God and rejoiced. I sank into sorrow in my thoughts, and my spirit failed.
My eyes were awake before the night watches. INTERLUDE. I was troubled and did not speak.
I considered the days of old, and I remembered the eternal years and meditated. Or he pondered.
At night I reflected in my heart, and my spirit searched deeply.
Will the Lord reject us forever, and never again show favor?
Will he cut off his mercy completely? Has he brought his word to an end for generation after generation?
Will God forget to show mercy? Will he withhold his compassion in his anger?
And I said, “Now I have begun; this is the change of the right hand of the Most High.”
I remembered the works of the Lord, for I will remember your wonders from the beginning.
And I will meditate on all your works and reflect on your deeds.
O God, your way is in the holy place. What god is as great as our God?
You are the God who works wonders. You have made your power known among the peoples.
With your arm you redeemed your people, the children of Jacob and Joseph. INTERLUDE.
The waters saw you, O God; the waters saw you and were afraid. The depths were troubled.
A great roar of waters. The clouds gave voice, for your arrows pass through.
The sound of your thunder was in the wheel. Your lightning lit up the world. The earth shook and trembled.
Your way is in the sea, and your path in the mighty waters, and your footsteps will not stumble.
You led your people like sheep by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
77. GLORY. HYMN SUNG WHILE SEATED. AN INSTRUCTION OF ASAPH.
Listen, my people, to my law. Incline your ear to the words of my mouth.
I will open my mouth in parables. I will proclaim riddles from the beginning.
All that we have heard and understood, our fathers have told us.
It was not hidden from their children in the next generation, as they proclaimed the praises of the Lord and his power and the wonders he had done.
And he established a testimony in Jacob and laid down a law in Israel, which he commanded our fathers to make known to their sons.
So that another generation may know—the children yet to be born—and they may rise and tell these things to their own children.
So that they may place their hope in God and not forget God's works, but seek his commandments.
So that they may not be like their fathers, a stubborn and provoking generation, a generation that did not set its heart right and whose spirit was not faithful to God.
The sons of Ephraim, drawing and shooting their bows, turned back on the day of battle.
They did not keep God's covenant and were unwilling to walk in his law.
And they forgot his goodness and the wonders that he had shown them.
The wonders that he performed before their fathers, in the land of Egypt, in the field of Tanis. The field's name is Zanios.
He split the sea and led them through; he held the waters as in a wineskin.
And he led them with a cloud by day, and all night with the light of fire.
He pierced and split the rock in the wilderness and gave them drink, as in a vast waterless place.
He brought water out of the rock and made waters flow down like rivers.
And they continued to sin against him; they provoked the Most High in the waterless place.
They tested God in their hearts by asking for food for themselves.
And they spoke against God and said, “Can God prepare a table in the wilderness?
Since he struck the rock and waters flowed and streams overflowed, can he also give bread or prepare a table for his people?”
Therefore the Lord heard and was provoked, and fire blazed in Jacob, and wrath [?] upon Israel.
Because they put their faith in God and did not trust in his salvation.
And he commanded the clouds [?] and opened the doors of heaven.
And he rained manna upon them to eat and gave them the bread of heaven.
Human beings ate the bread of angels; he sent them food in abundance.
He stirred up the south wind in heaven and brought the west wind by his power.
And he rained meat upon them like dust, and feathered birds like the sand of the sea.
And they fell in the midst of their camp, around their dwellings.
And they ate and were thoroughly satisfied, and he brought them what they desired.
They were not deprived of their desire, and the food was still in their mouths.
And God's anger rose against them, and he killed many of them and struck down the chosen men of Israel.
Despite all this, they sinned against him again and did not believe in his wonders.
And their days ended in futility, and their years in haste.
When he was killing them, they sought him; they turned back and came early to God.
And they remembered that God is my helper, and that God Most High is their deliverer.
They loved him with their mouths, but lied to him with their tongues.
Their hearts were not right with him, nor were they faithful to his commandment.
But he is merciful: he cleansed their sin and did not destroy them. He will repeatedly turn away his fury and will not kindle all his anger.
And he remembered that they are flesh, a breath that passes and does not return.
How often they angered him in the wilderness and provoked him in the waterless land!
And they turned back and tested God, and angered the Holy One of Israel.
They did not remember his hand, the day when he delivered them from the hand of their oppressor,
how he set signs in Egypt and his wonders in the plain of Tanis.
And he turned their rivers and their rain showers into blood, so that they could not drink.
He sent biting flies against them, and they devoured them, and frogs, which destroyed them.
And he gave their fruit to mildew; a beast [?], and decay [?] to locusts.
He struck their vines with hail and their mulberry trees with frost.
And he gave their livestock over to hail and their possessions to fire.
Mulberry trees. He sent against them the anger of his fury, fury and anger and distress, a sending of fierce angels.
He made a way, a path, for his anger. He did not spare their lives from death, and he shut their livestock up in death.
And he struck down all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, the first fruits of all their labor in the dwellings of Ham.
And he led his people out like sheep and brought them up like a flock in the wilderness.
And he guided them in hope, and they were not afraid; and the sea covered their enemies.
And he brought them to the mountain of his sanctuary, this mountain which his right hand acquired.
He drove out nations before them and divided the land among them by lot, with a measuring cord. And he settled the tribes of Israel in their dwellings.
They tested and angered God Most High and did not keep his decrees.
They turned back and rebelled like their fathers; they became like a warped bow.
They angered him with their high places and provoked him with their carved idols.
God heard and rejected them, and utterly despised Israel.
He rejected the tabernacle at Shiloh [?], the dwelling where he had lived among human beings.
He handed their strength over into captivity and their splendor into the hands of enemies.
He delivered his people over to the sword and despised his inheritance.
Fire devoured their young men, and their maidens were not mourned.
Their priests fell by the sword, and their widows were not mourned.
Then the Lord rose as though from sleep, like a mighty man roaring from wine.
He struck their enemies from behind and put them to everlasting shame.
He rejected Joseph’s dwelling and did not choose the tribe of Ephraim.
He chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion, which he loved.
He built his sanctuary like a unicorn; he established it on the earth forever.
He chose David his servant and took him from the flocks of sheep.
He took him from the nursing ewes to shepherd Jacob his servant and Israel his inheritance.
He shepherded them with an innocent heart and guided them with skillful hands. Glory.
78. A Psalm of Asaph.
O God, nations have entered your inheritance. They have defiled your holy temple; they have made Jerusalem like a storehouse for fruit.
They have laid out the corpses of your servants as food for the birds of heaven, the flesh of your faithful ones for the beasts of the earth.
They have poured out their blood like water around Jerusalem, and there was no one to bury them.
We have become a disgrace to our neighbors, an object of mockery and derision to those around us.
How long, Lord? Will you be angry forever? Will your jealousy burn like fire?
Pour out your anger on the nations that do not know you and on the kingdoms that have not called on your name.
For they have devoured Jacob and laid waste his dwelling place.
Do not remember our former lawless deeds. Let your mercies come quickly to meet us, Lord, for I have become very poor.
Help us, God our Savior. For the glory of your name, Lord, deliver us, and cleanse our sins for your name’s sake.
Will the nations ever say, “Where is their God?” Let vengeance for the shed blood of your servants become known among the nations before our eyes.
Let the groaning of the prisoners come before you. By the greatness of your arm, preserve the children of those put to death.
Repay our neighbors sevenfold into their laps for the insults with which they insulted you,
Lord. But we, your people and the sheep of your pasture, will give thanks to you forever. From generation to generation we will proclaim your praise.
79. For the end. Concerning those who are changed. A testimony. A psalm of Asaph. [?].
Shepherd of Israel, listen, you who lead Joseph like a sheep. You who sit upon the cherubim, reveal yourself.
Before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh, stir up your strength and come to save us.
God, turn us back, and let your face shine, and we will be saved.
Lord God, how long will you be angry at the prayer of your servants?
You will feed us with the bread of tears and give us tears to drink in measure.
You have made us a cause of strife among our neighbors, and our enemies have mocked us.
Lord God of hosts, turn us back, and let your face shine upon us, and we will be saved. Musical interlude.
You brought a vine out of Egypt; you drove out the nations and planted it.
You made a way before it, planted its roots, and it filled the earth.
Its shade covered the mountains, and its branches covered the cedars of God.
You stretched out its branches as far as [?], and its shoots as far as the river.
Why did you tear down its fence, so that everyone passing along the road plucks it?
A boar from the forest has ravaged it, and a solitary wild beast has devoured it.
God of hosts, turn back. Look down from heaven and see, and visit your vine,
and perfect what your right hand has planted; look also upon the son whom you have made strong for yourself.
It is burned with fire and dug up. At the rebuke of your face they will perish.
Let your hand be upon the man of your right hand, and upon the son of man whom you have made strong for yourself.
And we will not turn away from you. You will give us life, and we will call upon your name.
Lord God of hosts, turn us back. Let your face shine, and we shall be saved.
80. For the end. A psalm of Asaph, concerning the winepresses, for the fifth day of the week.
Rejoice in God our helper. Shout aloud to the God of Jacob.
Take up a psalm and sound the tambourine, the lovely psaltery together with harps.
Blow the trumpet at the new moon, on the appointed day of your feast.
For this is a commandment for Israel and an ordinance of the God of Jacob.
He established it as a testimony in Joseph when he went out from the land of Egypt. He heard a language he did not know.
He freed their backs from burdens; his hands labored with a basket.
In distress you called upon me, and I rescued you. I heard you in the hidden place of the storm. I tested you at the water of contention. Pause.
Listen, my people, and I will testify to you. Israel, if you would listen to me!
There shall be no new god among you, nor shall you bow down to a foreign god.
For I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt. Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.
But my people did not listen to my voice, and Israel paid no attention to me.
So I gave them over to the desires of their hearts; they will follow their own plans.
If only my people had listened to me, if only Israel had walked in my ways!
I would have humbled their enemies at once and laid my hand upon those who oppressed them.
The Lord’s enemies lied to him, and their time will last forever.
And [?] them with the finest wheat, and satisfied them with honey from a rock.
81. Glory. For the end. A psalm of Asaph.
God stood in the assembly of gods; in the midst of the gods he will judge.
How long will you judge unjustly and show favor to sinners? Pause.
Give justice to the orphan and the needy; uphold the rights of the lowly and the poor.
Rescue the poor and needy; deliver them from the hands of sinners.
They neither knew nor understood; they walk in darkness. Let all the foundations of the earth be shaken.
I said, “You shall be gods, and all of you sons of the Most High.”
But you will die like human beings and fall like one of the princes.
Rise up, O God, judge the earth, for you will take possession among all the nations.
82. A SONG. A PSALM OF ASAPH.
O God, who can compare with you? Do not remain silent or be still, O God.
For look, your enemies have raised an uproar, and those who hate you have lifted up their heads.
They plotted wickedly against your people [?] and conspired against your holy ones.
They said, “Come, let us wipe them out from among the nations, so that the name of Israel will be remembered no more.”
For they conspired together with one purpose; they made a covenant against you.
The tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagrites,
Gebal, Ammon, and Amalek; the foreigners, a company of foreigners, with those who live in Tyre. Pause [?].
For Assyria too joined them; they became a support to the sons of Lot.
Do to them as you did to Midian and Sisera, as to Jabin at the stream of Kishon.
They were destroyed at Endor; they became like dung on the ground.
Make their princes like Oreb and Zeeb, and all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna,
who said, “Let us take possession of God’s sanctuary for ourselves.”
O my God, make them like a wheel, like dry stalks before the wind.
As fire burns up forests, as a flame sets mountains ablaze,
so you will pursue them with your storm and throw them into confusion with your anger.
Fill their faces with disgrace, and they will seek your name, O Lord.
Let them be ashamed and bewildered forever and ever; let them be disgraced and perish.
And they will know that your name is the Lord; you alone are the Most High over all the earth.
83. FOR THE END. CONCERNING THE WINEPRESSES. A PSALM FOR THE SONS OF KORAH.
How beloved are your dwellings, O Lord of hosts!
My soul longs and faints for the courts of the Lord. My heart and my flesh rejoiced in the living God.
For the bird has found a home for itself, and the turtledove a nest for itself, where it has laid its young: your altars, O Lord of hosts, my King and my God. [?]
Blessed are those who live in your house; they will be praised forever and ever.
Blessed is the man whose help comes from you. He has set the paths of ascent in his heart.
In the valley of weeping, in the place he appointed. For the lawgiver will give blessings.
They will go from strength to strength; the God of gods will appear in Zion. Pause.
Lord God of hosts, hear my prayer. Listen, God of Jacob. Pause.
Look, O God, our protector, and look upon the face of your anointed one.
For one day in your courts is better than thousands. I chose to be an outcast in the house of my God rather than live in the dwellings of sinners.
For the Lord loves mercy and truth. God will give grace and glory. The Lord will not withhold good things from those who walk in innocence.
Lord God of hosts, blessed is the man who trusts in you.
84. For the end. For the sons of Korah. A psalm.
Lord, you have shown favor to your land; you have brought back the captives of Jacob.
You have forgiven the lawlessness of your people; you have covered all their sins. Pause.
15. You have restrained all your anger; you have turned away from your fierce wrath.
Turn us back, O God of our salvation, and turn your wrath away from us.
Will you be angry with us forever? Will you extend your anger from generation to generation?
O God, you will turn and give us life, and your people will rejoice in you.
Show us your mercy, Lord, and give us your salvation.
I will hear what the Lord God will say concerning me, for he will speak peace to his people, to his faithful ones, and to those who turn their hearts toward him.
Indeed, his salvation is near those who fear him, so that glory may dwell in our land.
Mercy and truth have met; righteousness and peace have kissed.
Truth has sprung up from the earth, and righteousness has looked down from heaven.
And God will give goodness, and our land will yield its fruit.
Righteousness will go before him and will set its footsteps on the path.
5. 15. Glory. [?] A prayer of David. Incline your ear, Lord, and hear me, for I am poor.
Preserve my soul, for I am faithful. Save your servant, my God, who trusts in you.
Have mercy on me, Lord, for I will cry out to you all day long.
Gladden the soul of your servant, for to you, Lord, I have lifted up my soul.
For you, Lord, are good and gentle, and full of mercy toward all who call upon you.
Give ear, Lord, to my prayer, and attend to the voice of my supplication.
In the day of my distress I cried out to you, for you heard me.
There is none like you among the gods, Lord, and there are no works like yours.
All the nations you have made will come and bow down before you, Lord, and glorify your name.
For you are great and work wonders; you alone are God.
Guide me, Lord, on your path, and I will walk in your truth. Let my heart rejoice in fearing your name.
I will give thanks to you, Lord my God, with all my heart, and I will glorify your name forever.
For your mercy toward me is great; you have delivered my soul from the depths of Hades.
O God, lawbreakers have risen against me, and a gathering of powerful men has sought my life. They have not set you before them.
But you, Lord my God, are compassionate and very merciful, patient and very merciful and true.
Look upon me and have mercy on me. Give your strength to your servant, and save the son of your maidservant.
Show me a sign of your goodness, so that those who hate me may see it and be ashamed, because you, Lord, have helped me and comforted me.
86. A psalm of the sons of Korah. Their foundations are on the holy mountains.
The Lord loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.
Glorious things are spoken of you, city of God. Musical interlude.
I will remember Rahab and Babylon [?] among those who know me. Behold, the foreigners and Tyre and the people of Ethiopia: these were born there.
A man will say, “Mother Zion,” and a man was born in her; and the Most High himself established her.
The Lord will record in the books of peoples and princes those who were born in her.
For the dwelling of all who rejoice is in you.
A psalm for the sons of Korah. For the end, concerning Mahalath, to answer, [?], for instruction, of Heman the Israelite.
87. Lord, God of my salvation, by day I cried out, and by night before you.
Let my prayer come before you; incline your ear to your supplication.
For my soul is filled with troubles, and my life has drawn near to Hades.
I was counted among those who go down into the pit; I became like a man
without help, free among the dead, like the wounded who sleep in graves, whom you remember no more, and who have been cast away from your hand.
They placed me in the deepest pit, in dark places, in the shadow of death.
Your wrath has settled upon me, and you have brought all your waves upon me.
You have removed my acquaintances far from me; they have made me an object of loathing to themselves. I was handed over and could not go out.
My eyes have grown weak from poverty. I cried to you, Lord, all day long; I lifted up my hands.
Will you work wonders for the dead? Or will physicians raise them up, and will they praise you?
Will anyone tell of your mercy in the grave, or of your faithfulness in destruction?
Will your wonders be known in darkness, and your righteousness in the land of forgetfulness?
But I cried to you, Lord, and in the morning my prayer will come before you.
Why, Lord, do you reject my soul? Why do you turn your face away from me?
I am poor and have been in hardship from my youth. When I was lifted up, I was humbled and became bewildered.
Your waves of anger passed over me; your terrors troubled me.
They surrounded me like water all day long; together they hemmed me in.
You have removed a close friend far from me, and my acquaintances because of my suffering.
88. Glory. Instruction concerning hidden things. Of Ethan the Israelite.
I will sing of your mercies forever, Lord; with my mouth I will proclaim your faithfulness from generation to generation.
As he said, mercy will be built up forever.
Your faithfulness will be established in the heavens. I made a covenant with my chosen ones; I swore to my chosen ones.
I will establish your descendants forever, and I will build up your throne from generation to generation. Musical interlude.
The heavens will praise your wonders, Lord, and your faithfulness in the assembly of the holy ones.
For who in the clouds can be compared to the Lord? Who among the sons of God can be likened to the Lord?
God is glorified among his holy ones; he is great and fearsome above all those around him.
Lord God of hosts, who is like you? You are mighty, Lord, and your faithfulness surrounds you.
You rule the might of the sea; you calm the surging of its waves.
You humbled [?] like a wounded man, and with your mighty arm you scattered your enemies.
The heavens are yours, and the earth is yours. You founded the inhabited world and its farthest reaches.
You created the north and the sea. Tabor and Hermon rejoiced in your name—that is, when they heard the voice from heaven.
Your arm is mighty. Let your hand be strengthened; let your right hand be exalted. This is my beloved Son.
Righteousness and justice are the foundation of your throne; mercy and truth go before your face.
Blessed are the people who know the joyful shout. Lord, they will walk in the light of your face.
And you will rejoice in your name all day long, and they will be exalted through righteousness.
For you are the glory of their strength, and through your favor our horn will be exalted.
For protection belongs to the Lord, and to the Holy One of Israel, our king.
Then you spoke in a vision to your sons and said, “I have placed help upon a mighty man; I have exalted one chosen from my people.
I have found David my servant; with my holy oil I have anointed him.
For my hand will help him, and my arm will strengthen him.
The enemy will gain nothing against him, and the son of lawlessness will no longer afflict him.
I will cut down his enemies before him, and I will defeat those who hate him.
My truth and my mercy will be with him, and in my name his horn will be exalted.
I will set his hand upon the sea, and his right hand upon the rivers.
He will call upon me: ‘You are my Father, my God, the defender of my salvation.’
And I will make him the firstborn, exalted above the kings of the earth.
I will preserve my mercy for him forever, and my covenant will remain faithful to him.
I will establish his descendants forever and ever, and his throne like the days of heaven.
If his sons abandon my law and do not walk according to my judgments,
if they profane my statutes and do not keep my commandments,
I will punish the lawless with a rod, and the unrighteous with blows.
But I will not withdraw my mercy from them, nor will I fail in my truth.
Nor will I profane my covenant, nor will I reject what has come from my lips.
Once I swore by my holiness: I will not lie to David.
His descendants will remain forever, and his throne will be like the sun before me,
and like the moon, established forever. The witness in heaven is faithful. Interlude.
But you have rejected and humiliated him; you have cast off your anointed one.
Or previously, you broke the covenant with your servant; you profaned his sanctuary on the ground.
You have broken down all his defenses; you have made his stronghold a place of terror.
Everyone passing along the road plundered him; he became an object of scorn to his neighbors.
You have raised the right hand of those who oppress him; you have made all his enemies rejoice.
You have turned away the help of his weapons, and you have not defended him on the day of battle.
You have stripped him of his purity; you have hurled his throne to the ground.
You have shortened the days of his life; you have covered him with shame. Interlude.
How long, Lord, will you turn away completely? Will your anger blaze like fire?
Remember what my existence is. Have you created the children of men in vain?
What person will live and not see death? Will he deliver his soul from the hand of Hades?
Where are your mercies of old, Lord, which you swore to David in your truth?
Remember, Lord, the insults against your servants, which I have borne in my heart from many nations.
Your enemies have hurled these insults, Lord; they have insulted the change of your anointed one.
Blessed is the Lord forever. So be it, so be it. Glory.
89. A PRAYER OF MOSES, THE MAN OF GOD. Lord, you have been our refuge from generation to generation.
Before the mountains came into being, and the earth and the inhabited world were created, from eternity to eternity you are.
Do not turn mankind back to humiliation. You said, “Return, children of men.”
For a thousand years in your sight, Lord, are like yesterday, which has passed, and like a watch in the night.
Their years will count for nothing; in the morning they will pass away like grass.
In the morning it will bloom and pass away; by evening it will fall, grow hard, and wither.
For we have been consumed by your anger, and thrown into confusion by your wrath.
You have set our lawless deeds before you, our lifetime in the light of your face.
For all our days have dwindled away, and we have been consumed by your anger. Our years were spent like a spider’s web.
The days of our years are seventy years, or, if we have strength, eighty years. Most of them are toil and pain, for gentleness has come upon us, and we shall be disciplined.
Who knows the power of your anger, and who can measure your wrath according to the fear of you?
Make your right hand known to me in this way, and those whose hearts are bound by wisdom.
Return, O Lord! How long? Be moved by the pleas of your servants. Comfort
We were filled with your mercy in the morning, O Lord, and we rejoiced and were glad. All our days we were glad,
in return for the days in which [?] you humbled us, the years in which we saw evil.
Look upon your servants and upon your works, and guide their children.
May the radiance of the Lord our God be upon us. Establish the work of our hands for us; establish the work of our hands.
A SONG OF PRAISE OF DAVID. Whoever lives with the help of the Most High will dwell under the shelter of the God of heaven.
He will say to God, “You are my protector and my refuge, my God; I trust in him.”
For he will rescue me from the hunter’s snare and from the troubling word.
He will shelter you with his shoulders, and under his wings you will find hope. His truth will surround you like a shield.
You will not be afraid of the terror of the night, or of the arrow that flies by day,
or of the thing that passes through the darkness, or of calamity and the demon of midday.
A thousand will fall at your side, and ten thousand at your right hand, but it will not come near you.
You will only look with your eyes and see the repayment of sinners.
For you, O Lord, are my hope. You have made the Most High your refuge.
No evil will come to you, and no plague will approach your body.
For he will command his angels concerning you, to guard you in all your ways.
They will lift you up in their hands, so that you never strike your foot against a stone.
You will tread upon the asp and the basilisk, and trample the lion and the serpent.
Because he has trusted in me, I will rescue him. I will shelter him, because he has known my name.
He will call to me, and I will hear him. I am with him in trouble. I will rescue him and glorify him.
I will satisfy him with a long life and show him my salvation.
Glory. [?] A psalm. A song for the Sabbath day. 91.
It is good to give thanks to the Lord and to sing to your name, Most High,
to proclaim your mercy in the morning and your faithfulness every night,
on a ten-stringed psaltery, with a song sung aloud.
For you have made me great, Lord, through your creation, and I will rejoice in the works of your hands.
How great your works have become, Lord! Your thoughts have become very deep.
A foolish man does not know, and a senseless man does not understand these things.
When sinners sprout like grass and all who practice lawlessness spring up—16. Bast shoe.—it is so that they may be destroyed forever and ever.
But you, Lord, are on high forever.
For look, your enemies, Lord—for look, your enemies will perish, and all who practice lawlessness will be scattered.
My horn will be raised like that of a unicorn, a mighty beast, and my old age will be rich in oil.
My eye has looked upon my enemies, and my ear will hear those who rise against me and act wickedly.
The righteous man will blossom like a palm tree, and they will multiply like the cedars of Lebanon, the yew trees.
Planted in the house of the Lord, they will blossom in the courts of our God.
They will still flourish in ripe old age.
They will prosper, so that they may proclaim that the Lord our God is upright and that there is no injustice in him.

David’s songs of praise, on the day before the Sabbath, when the earth was inhabited. 92. The Lord has become king; he has clothed himself in splendor. The Lord has clothed himself in strength and girded himself. For he has established the inhabited world, which will not be shaken.
Your throne has been established since then, and you are forever.
The rivers will rise, Lord; the rivers will raise their voices; the rivers will lift their currents at the sound of many waters.
The heights of the sea are wondrous; the Lord on high is wondrous.
Your testimonies have proved utterly trustworthy. Holiness befits your house, Lord, for all the days to come.
A psalm of David, for the fourth day of the week. 93. The Lord is a God of vengeance; the God of vengeance has not held back.
Rise up, judge of the earth; repay the proud what they deserve.
How long, Lord, how long will sinners boast?
They speak out and utter injustice; all who practice lawlessness speak.
They have humbled your people, Lord, and afflicted your inheritance.
They have put the widow and the orphan to death, and killed the foreigner.
And they said, “The Lord will not see, nor will the God of Jacob understand.”
Understand, you senseless people! And you fools, when will you become wise?
Does the one who planted the ear not hear? Does the one who formed the eye not see?
Will the one who disciplines nations not rebuke—the one who teaches people knowledge?
The Lord knows human thoughts, that they are futile.
Blessed is the person whom you discipline, Lord, and whom you teach from your law,
to give him rest from harsh days, until a pit is dug for the sinner.
For the Lord will not reject his people, nor will he abandon his inheritance,
until righteousness returns to judgment, and all the upright in heart cling to it.
Who will rise up for me against evildoers? Who will stand with me against those who practice lawlessness?
If the Lord had not helped me, my soul would soon have settled in Hades.
When I said, “My foot is slipping,” your mercy, Lord, supported me.
As the sorrows within my heart multiplied, your consolations brought me joy.
Can a throne of lawlessness be joined to you, one that creates hardship by decree?
They will hunt down the life of the righteous and condemn innocent blood.
And you, Lord, became my refuge, and my God became the help in which I hope.
And the Lord will repay them for their lawlessness, and according to their wickedness the Lord our God will destroy them. Glory.
94. A SONG OF PRAISE BY DAVID. Come, let us rejoice in the Lord; let us shout to God our Savior.
Let us come before his face with thanksgiving, and shout to him with psalms.
For God is great, and the Lord, and a great King over all the earth.
For the ends of the earth are in his hand, and the mountain heights are his.
For the sea is his, and he made it; his hands formed the dry land.
Come, let us worship and fall down before him, and let us weep before the Lord who made us.
For he is our God, and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in the provocation, on the day of testing in the wilderness,
where your fathers tested me; they tested me and saw my works.
For forty years I was displeased with that generation, and I said, “They always go astray in their hearts.” They did not know my ways,
so I swore in my anger, “They shall not enter my rest.”

95. When the temple was being built, [?] captivity. A psalm of David.
Sing a new song to the Lord; sing to the Lord, all the earth.
Sing to the Lord and bless his name; proclaim his salvation day after day.
Declare his glory among the nations, his wonders among all works.
For God is great and greatly to be praised; he is to be feared above all gods.
For all the gods of the nations are demons, but the Lord made the heavens. Praise and beauty are before him.
Holiness and splendor are in his sanctuary.
Bring to the Lord, you families of the nations.
Bring glory and honor to the Lord; bring to the Lord the glory due his name. Bring offerings and enter his courts.
Worship the Lord in his holy court; let all the earth tremble before him.
Say among the nations, “The Lord reigns.” For he established the world so that it will not be shaken. He will judge the peoples justly.
Let the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice; let the sea and all that fills it stir.

The fields and everything in them will rejoice. Then all the trees of the forest will rejoice before the Lord, for he is coming. For he is coming to judge the earth, to judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with his truth.

96. A song of David, when his land was put in order.
The Lord reigns; let the earth rejoice. Let the many fathers rejoice.
Cloud and darkness surround him; righteousness and judgment are the foundation of his throne.
Fire goes before him and burns up his enemies all around.
His lightning lit up the world; the earth saw it and trembled.
The mountains melted like wax before the Lord, before the Lord of all the earth.
The heavens proclaimed his righteousness, and all the peoples saw his glory.
Let all who worship carved images be put to shame, all who boast in their idols. Worship him, all his angels.
Zion heard and was glad, and the daughters of Judah rejoiced,
because of your judgments, Lord. For you are the Lord Most High over all the earth; you are exalted far above all gods.
You who love the Lord, hate evil. The Lord guards the souls of his faithful ones; he will rescue them from the hands of sinners.
Light has dawned for the righteous, and gladness for the upright in heart.
Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous, and give thanks at the remembrance of his holiness. Glory.
A PSALM OF DAVID. Sing a new song to the Lord, for the Lord has done wonderful things. His right hand and his holy arm have saved him.
The Lord has made his salvation known; he has revealed his righteousness before the nations.
He remembered his mercy toward Jacob and his faithfulness toward the house of Israel. All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.
Shout to the Lord, all the earth; sing, rejoice, and make music.
Sing to our God with harps, with harps and the sound of psalm singing.
With hammered trumpets and the sound of a horn, shout before the King, the Lord.
Let the sea and all that fills it be stirred, the inhabited world and all who live in it.
The rivers will clap their hands together; the mountains will rejoice before the Lord, for he is coming.
For he will come to judge the earth, to judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with fairness.
98. A PSALM OF DAVID. The Lord reigns; let the peoples be angry. He sits upon the cherubim; let the earth shake.
The Lord is great in Zion and exalted above all peoples.
Let them give thanks to your great name, for he is fearsome and holy.
And the king's honor loves justice. You have established uprightness; you have carried out justice and righteousness in Jacob.
Exalt the Lord our God and worship at his footstool, for he is holy.
Moses and Aaron were among his priests, and Samuel among those who called upon his name. They called upon the Lord, and he heard them.
He spoke to them in a pillar of cloud, for they kept his testimonies and the commands he gave them.
Lord our God, you answered them. God, you were merciful to them, yet you punished all their deeds.
Exalt the Lord our God and worship on his holy mountain, for the Lord our God is holy.
99. A PSALM OF DAVID, FOR THANKSGIVING. Shout to God, all the earth.
Serve the Lord with gladness. Come before him with joy.
Know that the Lord is our God. He made us, and not we ourselves. We are his people and the sheep of his pasture.
Enter his gates with thanksgiving and his courts with songs. Give thanks to him; praise his name.
For the Lord is good; his mercy lasts forever, and his faithfulness extends to every generation.
100. A Psalm of David. I will sing to you, Lord, of mercy and judgment.
I will sing and seek understanding in the blameless way. When will you come to me? I walked with an innocent heart within my house.
I set no lawless thing before my eyes. I hated those who committed transgression. A deceitful heart did not cling to me.
I did not know the evil man who turned away from me.
I drove out anyone who secretly slandered his neighbor. I would not eat with anyone who had a proud eye and an insatiable heart.
My eyes were on the faithful of the land, to seat them with me. Whoever walked in the blameless way served me.
No one who practiced arrogance lived within my [?]. Anyone who spoke unjust things did not prosper before my eyes.
Every morning I destroyed all the sinners of the land, to wipe out from the Lord’s city all who practiced lawlessness. Glory.
101. 17. A prayer of a poor man when he grows faint and pours out his prayer before the Lord.
Lord, hear my prayer, and let my cry come to you.
Do not turn your face away from me. On the day when I am in distress, incline your ear to me. On the day when I call upon you, hear me quickly.
For my days have vanished like smoke, and my bones have dried up like dry wood.
I was struck down like grass, and my heart withered, for I forgot to eat my bread.
Because of the sound of my groaning, my bones clung to my flesh.
I became like a pelican in the wilderness, like a night raven among the ruins.
I lay awake and became like a bird sitting alone on a rooftop.
All day long my enemies taunted me, and those who boasted about me swore oaths.
For I ate ashes like bread and mixed my drink with weeping,
because of your anger and your wrath, for you lifted me up and cast me down.
My days faded like a shadow, and I withered like grass.
But you, Lord, remain forever, and your remembrance endures from generation to generation.
You will arise and have mercy on Zion, for it is time to have mercy on her; the time has come.
For your servants cherish her stones and will show tenderness toward her dust.
The nations will fear the name of the Lord, and all the kings of the earth your glory.
For the Lord will rebuild Zion and appear in his glory.
He looked upon the prayer of the humble and did not despise their plea.
Let these things be written for another generation, and a people yet to be created will praise the Lord.
For he looked down from his holy height; the Lord looked upon the earth from heaven,
to hear the groaning of the prisoners and release the children of those put to death,
to proclaim the Lord’s name in Zion and his praise in Jerusalem,
when the peoples gather together, and kings gather to serve the Lord.
He answered him in the course of his strength: “Tell me how few my days are.
Do not take me away halfway through my days. Your years endure from generation to generation.
In the beginning, you, Lord, laid the earth’s foundation, and the heavens are the work of your hands.
They will perish, but you remain. They will all wear out like a garment; like a covering you will roll them up, and they will be changed.
But you are the same, and your years will come to an end.
The children of your servants will rejoice, and their descendants will be established forever.”
Psalm 102. Of David. Bless the Lord, my soul, and let everything within me bless his holy name.
Bless the Lord, my soul, and [?] do not forget all his benefits.
He forgives all your sins and heals all your illnesses.
He redeems your life from decay and crowns you with mercy and compassion.
He satisfies your desire with good things; your youth will be renewed like an eagle’s.
The Lord acts mercifully and gives justice to all who are wronged.
He made his ways known to Moses, your wishes to the children of Israel.
The Lord is compassionate and merciful, patient and abundant in mercy.
He will not remain angry to the end, nor will he bear hostility forever.
He has not dealt with us according to our lawless deeds, nor will he repay us according to our sins.
For as high as heaven is above the earth, so firmly has the Lord established his mercy toward those who fear him.
As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our lawless deeds from us.
As a father has compassion on his children, so will the Lord have compassion on those who fear him.
For he knows how we were made; he remembered that we are dust.
A person's days are like grass; like a flower, so will he bloom.
For a wind will pass through him, and he will be no more, and he will no longer know his place.
But the Lord's mercy is from everlasting to everlasting upon those who fear him.
And his righteousness is upon children's children, upon those who keep his covenant and remember his commandments to carry them out.
The Lord has established his throne in heaven, and his kingdom rules over all.
Bless the Lord, all his angels, mighty in strength, who carry out his word, listening to the voice of his words.
Bless the Lord, all his hosts, his servants who carry out his will.
Bless the Lord, all his works, in every place of his dominion. To glory on high. Bless the Lord, O my soul. Glory.

103. A Psalm of David, concerning the creation of the whole world. Bless the Lord, O my soul. O Lord my God, you have become exceedingly great. He clothed himself in praise and splendor, wrapping himself in light as in a robe.
He stretches out heaven like a hide and covers its upper chambers with water.
He makes the clouds his means of ascent and walks on the wings of the wind.
He makes his angels spirits and his servants a blazing fire.
He establishes the earth on its firm foundation; it will not be shaken forever and ever.
The deep is its covering, like a robe; the waters will stand above the mountains.
At your rebuke they will flee; at the sound of your thunder they will be afraid.
They rise up the mountains and descend into the plain, to the place you established for them.
You set a boundary that they will not cross, nor will they return to cover the earth.
He sends springs into the valleys; the waters will flow between the mountains.
They will give drink to all the wild animals; wild donkeys await them in their thirst.
Beside them the birds of heaven will dwell; from among the rocks they will give voice.
You water the mountains from your upper chambers; the earth is filled with the fruit of your works.
You make grass grow for livestock and plants for human use, to bring forth bread from the earth.
And wine gladdens the human heart, oil makes the face shine, and bread strengthens the human heart.
The trees of the field are filled, the cedars of Lebanon that you planted. Stork.
There the birds will nest; the heron's dwelling rules over them.
The high mountains are for deer; the rock is a refuge for hares.
You made the moon to mark the seasons; the sun knows its setting.
You established darkness, and night came, when all the beasts of the forest go about.
Lion cubs roar to seize prey and to ask God for their food.
The sun rises, and they gather together and lie down in their dens.
A person goes out to work and labors until evening.
How great your works have become, Lord! You made them all with wisdom; the earth is filled with your creation.
Here is the great, wide sea; there are creeping creatures beyond number, living things both small and great.
There ships sail across, and there is this dragon that you created to play in it.
All look to you to give them food at the proper time.
When you give to them, they gather it; when you open your hand, all things are filled with goodness.
When you turn your face away, they are troubled. You take away their spirit, and they perish and return to their dust.
You send out your Spirit, and they are created, and you renew the face of the earth.
May the Lord's glory last forever; the Lord will rejoice in his works.
He looks upon the earth and makes it tremble; he touches the mountains, and they smoke.
I will sing to the Lord throughout my life; I will sing to my God as long as I exist.
May my words be pleasing to him; I will rejoice in the Lord.
May sinners perish from the earth, and may the lawless cease to exist. GLORY. Bless the Lord, my soul. ALLELUIA.
104. Give thanks to the Lord and call upon his name; proclaim his deeds among the nations.
Sing to him and sing praises to him; tell of his wonders among all peoples.
Glory in his holy name; let the hearts of those who seek the Lord rejoice.
Seek the Lord and be strengthened; seek his face continually.
Remember the wonders he has done, his marvelous deeds and the judgments of his mouth.
You offspring of Abraham, his servants, you sons of Jacob, his chosen ones.
He is the Lord our God; his judgments are throughout the earth.
He remembered his covenant forever, the word he commanded for a thousand generations,
which he established with Abraham, and his oath to Isaac.
He established it for Jacob as a decree, and for Israel as an everlasting covenant,
saying, “To you I will give the land of Canaan as the allotment of your inheritance.”
For they were few in number, only a few foreigners in it.
They passed from nation to nation, and from one kingdom to another people.
He allowed no one to mistreat them, and he rebuked kings on their behalf:
“Do not touch my anointed ones, and do not act wickedly against my prophets.”
He called a famine upon the land; he broke every supply of bread [?].
He sent a man ahead of them: Joseph was sold into slavery.
They confined his feet in shackles; iron pierced his soul.
Until his word came to pass, the word of the Lord tested [?] him.
The king sent and released him; the ruler of peoples set him free.
He made him lord of his house and ruler over all his possessions,
so that he might teach his princes to be like himself and make his elders wise.
Israel entered Egypt, and Jacob came to the land of Ham.
He greatly increased his people and made them stronger than their enemies.
He turned his own heart to hate his people and to deal deceitfully with his servants.
He sent Moses his servant, and Aaron, whom he had chosen for himself.
He placed in them the words of his signs and of his wonders in the land of Ham.
He sent darkness, and it grew dark, because they had defied his words.
He turned their waters into blood and killed their fish.
Their land teemed with frogs, even in their kings’ treasuries.
He spoke, and biting flies came, and gnats throughout their territory.
He made their rain into hail, with fire burning through their land.
He struck their vineyards and their fig trees and shattered every tree within their borders.
He spoke, and locusts came, and caterpillars without number.
They ate all the grass in their land and devoured all the produce of their land.
He killed all the firstborn in their land, the firstfruits of all their labor.
He brought them out with silver and gold, and there was no sickness among their tribes.
Egypt rejoiced at their departure, because fear of them had fallen upon the Egyptians.
He spread clouds as a covering for them, and fire to give them light at night.
They asked, and quails came, and he satisfied them with bread from heaven.
He split open a rock, and waters flowed out; rivers flowed through waterless places.
For he remembered his holy word, which he had given to Abraham his servant.
He brought out his people with joy, and his chosen ones with gladness.
