He gave them the lands of the nations, and they inherited the labor of other peoples.
So that they might keep his ordinances and seek his law. Glory. Sessional hymn. Alleluia.
105. Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever.
Who can proclaim the mighty deeds of the Lord and make all his praises heard?
Blessed are those who uphold justice and do what is right at all times. [?]
Remember us, Lord, when you show favor to your people; visit us with your salvation.
So that we may see the prosperity of your chosen ones, rejoice in the gladness of your nation, and glory with your inheritance.
We have sinned with our fathers; we have acted lawlessly and have not done what is right. [?]
Our fathers in Egypt did not understand your wonders. They did not remember the abundance of your mercy, and they provoked you to anger as they entered the Red Sea.
And he saved them for his name’s sake, to make his power known to them.
And he rebuked the Red Sea, and it dried up; and he led them through the depths as through a wilderness.
And he saved them from the hands of those who hated them, and delivered them from the hands of their enemies.
The water covered those who oppressed them; not one of them survived.
And they believed his word and sang praise to him.
They quickly forgot his deeds; they did not keep his counsel.
And they craved intensely in the wilderness, and tested God in the waterless land.
And he gave them what they asked for, and sent fullness into their souls.
And they angered Moses in the camp, and Aaron, the holy one of the Lord.
The earth opened and swallowed Dathan, and covered the assembly of Abiram.
And fire broke out in their assembly; a flame burned up the sinners.
And they made a calf at Horeb, and worshiped a cast image.
And they exchanged his glory for the image of a calf that eats hay.
And they forgot God, who saved them, who had done great things in Egypt,
wonders in the land of Ham, and terrifying deeds at the Red Sea.
And he said, “I will destroy them,” had not Moses, his chosen one, stood in the breach before him to turn away his wrath, so that he would not destroy them.
And they despised the desirable land; they did not believe his word.
And they grumbled in their tents; they did not listen to the voice of the Lord.
And he raised his hand against them, to strike them down in the wilderness,
and to strike down their descendants among the nations, and scatter them throughout the lands.
And they joined themselves to Baal-peor; they defiled themselves in [?], and ate sacrifices offered to the dead.
And they provoked him by their deeds, and death spread among them.
And Phinehas stood up and made atonement, and the slaughter stopped.
And it was credited to him as righteousness, from generation to generation forever.
And they angered him at the waters of strife, and Moses suffered because of them.
For they angered his spirit, and he spoke rashly with his lips.
They did not destroy the nations as the Lord had told them to do.
They mingled with the nations and learned their practices.
They served their carved idols, which became a snare to them.
They sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons.
They shed innocent blood, the blood of their sons and daughters [?], whom they sacrificed to the carved idols of Canaan, and the land was slain through bloodshed.
They defiled themselves by their deeds and prostituted themselves through their practices.
The Lord became fiercely angry with his people, and he loathed his own inheritance.
He handed them over to their enemies, and those who hated them ruled over them.
Their enemies oppressed them, and they were humbled beneath their hands.
Many times he delivered them, but they angered him with their own schemes and were brought low through their lawless deeds.
The Lord saw when they were in distress, and he heard their prayer.
He remembered his covenant and relented according to the abundance of his mercy.
He caused them to receive mercy from all who had taken them captive.
Save us, O Lord our God, and gather us from among the nations, so that we may give thanks to your holy name and glory in your praise.
Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, forever and ever. And all the people shall say, “So be it! So be it!” Glory. Alleluia.
106. Give thanks to the Lord, for he is [?], for his mercy endures forever.
Let those redeemed by the Lord say so, those whom he redeemed from the enemy’s hand.
He gathered them from the lands, from the east and the west, from the north and the sea.
They wandered in a waterless wilderness. They found a road to an inhabited city.
Hungry and thirsty, their souls grew faint within them.
They cried out to the Lord when they were in distress, and he delivered them from their troubles.
He led them along a straight road to enter an inhabited city.
Let them give thanks to the Lord for his mercy and for his wonderful deeds for humankind.
For he has satisfied the empty soul and filled the hungry soul with good things.
Those who sat in darkness and the shadow of death, bound in poverty and iron,
because they had defied the words of God and rejected the counsel of the Most High.
Their hearts were humbled by hardship; they grew weak, and there was no one to help.
Then they cried out to the Lord in their distress, and he saved them from their troubles.
He brought them out of darkness and the shadow of death and broke their bonds.
Let them thank the Lord for his mercy and for his wonderful deeds for humankind.
For he shattered the bronze gates and broke the iron bars.
He took them away from the path of their lawlessness, for they had been brought low because of their lawless deeds.
Their souls loathed all food, and they drew near to the gates of death.
Then they cried out to the Lord in their distress, and he rescued them from their troubles.
He sent his word and healed them, and rescued them from their destruction.
Let them thank the Lord for his mercy and for his wonderful deeds for humankind.
Let them offer him a sacrifice of praise and proclaim his deeds with joy.
Those who go down to the sea in ships, doing business on the great waters,
they saw the deeds of the Lord and his wonders in the deep.
He spoke, and a stormy wind arose, and the sea’s waves rose high.
They rose to the heavens and sank to the depths; their souls melted in their misery.
They reeled and staggered like drunken people, and all their wisdom was swallowed up.
Then they cried out to the Lord in their distress, and he rescued them from their troubles and brought them out.
He commanded the storm, and it became a gentle breeze, and the sea’s waves fell silent.
They rejoiced because the waves had fallen silent, and he guided them to their desired harbor.
Let them thank the Lord for his mercy and for his wonderful deeds for humankind.
Let them exalt him in the assembly of the people and praise him in the council of the elders.
You have turned rivers into a desert and springs of water into thirsty ground,
a fruitful land into a salt marsh, because of the wickedness of those who live in it.
You turned the wilderness into pools of water and the waterless land into springs of water.
He settled the hungry there, and they established cities to live in.
They sowed fields and planted vineyards, and produced a harvest of grain.
He blessed them, and they multiplied greatly; he did not let their livestock diminish.
They dwindled and were afflicted by distress, evils, and suffering.
Contempt was poured out upon their princes. He made them wander in a trackless place, not on a road.
He will help the poor out of poverty, and he made their families like flocks of sheep.
The righteous will see and rejoice, and all lawlessness will shut its mouth.
Who is wise enough to observe these things? They will understand the mercies of the Lord. Glory...
107. Praise. A song of David.
My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready. I sing and will sing praises in my glory.
Awake, my glory! Awake, psaltery and harp!
I will rise early. I will give thanks to you among the peoples, O Lord; I will sing praises to you among the nations.
For your mercy is great above the heavens, and your truth reaches to the clouds.
Be exalted, O God, [?] the heavens, and let your glory be over all the earth.
So that your beloved may be delivered, O Lord, save with your right hand and hear me.
God has spoken in his holy place: I will rejoice and divide Shechem, and measure out the Valley of Settlements.
Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine; Ephraim is the defense of my head.
Judah is my king. Moab is the basin of my hope. I will throw my sandal upon Edom. The foreigners have submitted to me.
Who will lead me into the fortified city? Who will guide me to Edom?
Is it not you, O God, who have rejected us and will not go out, O God, with our armies?
Give us help in distress, for human deliverance is futile.
With God we will act mightily, and he will bring our enemies to nothing.
108. For the end. A psalm of David. O God of my praise, do not remain silent.
For the mouth of the sinner and the deceitful mouth have opened against me. They have spoken against me with a deceitful tongue.
They surrounded me with hateful words and fought against me without cause.
In return for my love they slandered me, but I prayed.
They repaid me with evil for good, and with hatred for my love.
Set a wicked man over him, and let the devil stand at his right hand.
When he is tried, let him come away condemned, and let his prayer count as sin.
Let his days be few, and let another take his office.
Let his sons be orphans and his wife a widow.
Let his sons wander about and cry out, and let them be driven from their homes.
Let the creditor search out everything he owns, and let strangers plunder the fruits of his labor.
Let there be no one to defend him, and no one to have mercy on his orphans.
Let his children be destroyed; let his name be wiped out within a single generation.
Let the lawlessness of his fathers be remembered before the Lord, and let his mother's sin not be cleansed away.
Let these remain before the Lord always, and let their memory be wiped from the earth.
For he did not remember to show mercy, but persecuted the poor and needy man, seeking to kill the brokenhearted.
He loved a curse, and it came upon him; he did not desire a blessing, and it went far from him.
He clothed himself in a curse as in a robe, and it entered his body like water and his bones like oil.
Let it be to him like a robe he puts on, and like a belt he always wears.
This is the work of those who slander me to the Lord and speak evil against my soul.
But you, Lord, Lord, act on my behalf for your name's sake, for your mercy is good.
Deliver me, for I am poor and needy, and my heart is troubled within me.
Like a shadow as it fades, I am taken away; I am shaken off like locusts.
My knees have grown weak from fasting, and my flesh has wasted away for lack of oil.
I became an object of scorn to them. 19. When they saw me, they shook their heads.
Help me, Lord my God, and save me according to your mercy.
Let them know that this is your hand, and that you, Lord, have done it.
They will curse, but you will bless. Those who rise against me will be put to shame, but your servant will rejoice.
Those who slander me will be clothed in shame; they will wrap themselves in their disgrace as in a garment.
I will give great thanks to the Lord with my mouth, and I will praise him among many people.
For he stood at the right hand of the poor man, to save my soul from those who pursue it.
109. Glory. [?] A psalm of David. The Lord said to my lord, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for my feet.”
The Lord will send you a scepter of power from Zion, and you will prevail among your enemies.
Dominion is with you on the day of your distress, in the splendor of your holy ones. [?] the womb, before the morning star, I begot you.
The Lord has sworn and will not change his mind: “You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.”
The Lord at your right hand has crushed kings on the day of his wrath.
He will judge the nations and fill them with the fallen; he will crush heads over a vast land.
He will drink from a stream along the way; therefore he will lift up his head. Alleluia.
110. I will give thanks to you, Lord, with all my heart, in the council of the upright
and in the assembly. Great are the works of the Lord, sought out in all his purposes.
His works are praise and splendor, and his righteousness endures forever and ever.
He has made his wonders remembered. The Lord is merciful and compassionate.
He has given food to those who fear him. He will remember his covenant forever.
He will declare the power of his works to his people, to give them his own inheritance of the nations.
The works of your hands are truth and justice. All his commandments are trustworthy,
established forever and ever, made in truth and uprightness.
He sent redemption to his people; he ordained his covenant forever. Holy and fearsome is his name.
The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord. All who practice it have good understanding. His praise endures forever and ever. Alleluia.
111. Blessed is the man who fears the Lord; he will delight greatly in his commandments.
His offspring will be mighty on earth; the generation of the upright will be blessed.
Glory and wealth are in his house, and his righteousness endures forever and ever.
Light has dawned in the darkness for the upright; he is merciful, compassionate, and righteous.
A good man shows mercy and gives; he will consider his words in judgment.
For he will never be shaken; the righteous man will be remembered forever.
He will not fear bad news; his heart is ready to trust in the Lord.
His heart is firm; he will not be shaken until he looks upon his enemies.
He has distributed his gifts and given to the poor; his righteousness endures forever and ever. His horn will be raised in glory.
The sinner will see this and become angry; he will gnash his teeth and bark. The sinner’s desire will perish. Glory. Alleluia.
112. Praise the Lord, you servants; praise the name of the Lord.
Blessed be the name of the Lord, from now on and forever.
From the rising of the [?] to its setting, the name of the Lord is worthy of praise.
The Lord is high above all nations; his glory is above the heavens.
Who is like the Lord our God, who dwells on high
and looks upon the lowly things in heaven and on earth?
He raises the needy from the earth and lifts the poor from the dung heap,
to seat him with princes, with the princes of his people.
He settles the barren woman in a home as a mother rejoicing in her children. Alleluia.
113. When Israel went out of Egypt, the house of Jacob from a people of foreign speech,
Judah became his sanctuary, and Israel his dominion.
The sea saw and fled; the Jordan turned back.
The mountains skipped like rams, and the hills like lambs.
What happened to you, sea, that you fled, and to you, Jordan, that you turned back?
Mountains, why did you skip like rams, and hills, like lambs?
The earth shook before the Lord, before the God of Jacob,
who turned the rock into pools of water and the flint into springs of water.
Not to us, Lord, not to us, but to your name give glory, because of your mercy and your truth,
lest the nations ever say, “Where is their God?”
Our God is in heaven and on earth; he has done everything he wished.
The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the work of human hands.
They have mouths but do not speak; they have eyes but do not see.
They have ears but do not hear; they have nostrils but do not smell.
They have hands but do not feel; they have feet but do not walk; they make no sound with their throats.
May those who make them become like them, and all who trust in them.
The house of Israel trusted in the Lord; he is their helper and protector.
The house of Aaron trusted in the Lord; he is its helper and protector.
Those who fear the Lord trusted in the Lord; he is their helper and protector.
The Lord remembered us and blessed us. He has blessed the house of Israel; he has blessed the house of Aaron.
He has blessed those who fear the Lord, the small together with the great.
May the Lord give you increase, you and your children.
You are blessed by the Lord, who made heaven and earth. The heaven of heavens belongs to the Lord.
Heavens [?]. But he gave the earth to the children of humankind.
The dead will not praise you, Lord, nor will any who go down into Hades.
But we who are living will bless the Lord, from now and forever. Alleluia.
114. I have loved, for the Lord will hear the voice of my supplication.
For he will incline his ear to me, and I will call upon him throughout my days.
The pains of death surrounded me; the perils of Hades found me. I found distress and pain, and I called upon the name of the Lord.
O Lord, deliver my soul. The Lord is merciful and righteous, and our God shows mercy.
The Lord protects little children. I was brought low, and he saved me.
Return, my soul, to your rest, for the Lord has dealt kindly with you.
For he delivered my soul from death, my eyes from tears, and my feet from stumbling.
I will be pleasing before the Lord in the land of the living. Glory. Alleluia.
115. I believed; therefore I spoke.
But I was brought very low. I said in my dismay, “Everyone is a liar.”
What shall I give back to the Lord for all that he will give me?
I will take the cup of salvation and call upon the name of the Lord.
I will fulfill my vows to the Lord before all his people.
Precious before the Lord is the death of his faithful ones.
O Lord, I am your servant. I am your servant and the son of your servant woman. You have broken my bonds.
I will offer you a sacrifice of praise and call upon the name of the Lord.
I will fulfill my vows to the Lord before all his people.
In the courts of the Lord’s house, in your midst, Jerusalem. Hallelujah!
116. Praise the Lord, all nations! Praise him, all peoples!
For his mercy toward us has been firmly established, and the Lord’s truth endures forever. Hallelujah!
117. Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever.
Let the house of Israel now say that he is good, for his mercy endures forever.
Let the house of Aaron now say that he is good, for his mercy endures forever.
Let all who fear the Lord now say that he is good, for his mercy endures forever.
In my distress I called upon the Lord, and he answered me by bringing me into an open place.
The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what anyone may do to me.
The Lord is my helper, and I will look upon my enemies.
It is better to trust in the Lord than to trust in a human being.
It is better to put your hope in the Lord than to put your hope in princes.
All nations surrounded me, and in the name of the Lord I resisted them.
They encircled me and surrounded me; in the name of the Lord I resisted them.
They surrounded me like bees around a honeycomb, and they blazed like fire among thorns; in the name of the Lord I resisted them.
I was pushed and was about to fall, but the Lord took hold of me.
The Lord is my strength and my song, and he has become my salvation.
The sound of joy and salvation is in the dwellings of the righteous.
The Lord’s right hand has done mighty deeds. The Lord’s right hand has lifted me up. The Lord’s right hand has done mighty deeds.
I will not die, but will live and proclaim the Lord’s deeds.
The Lord showed me [?], and will not hand me over to death.
Open the gates of righteousness for me. I will enter them and give thanks to the Lord.
This is the Lord’s gate; the righteous will enter through it.
I will give thanks to you, because you have heard me and have become my salvation.
The stone that the builders considered worthless has become the cornerstone.
This came from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes.
This is the day the Lord has made. Let us rejoice and be glad in it.
O Lord, save! O Lord, grant success!
Blessed is he who comes in the Lord’s name. We have blessed you [?] from the Lord’s house.
God is the Lord, and he has shone upon us. Arrange the festival with leafy branches, up to the horns of the altar.
You are my God, and I will give thanks to you. You are my God, and I will exalt you. I will give thanks to you, because you have heard me and have become my salvation.
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever. Glory. [?] Alleluia.
118. Blessed are those whose way is blameless, who walk in the Lord’s law.
Blessed are those who search out his testimonies; they will seek him with all their heart.
For those who do no lawless deeds have walked in his ways.
You have commanded that your commandments be kept diligently.
Oh, that my ways might be set right [?], so that I may keep your statutes!
Then I will not be put to shame, O God, when I look upon all your commandments.
I will give thanks to you with an upright heart when I learn your righteous judgments.
I will keep your statutes; do not abandon me completely.
How can a young man set his way right? By keeping your words.
With all my heart I have sought you. Do not cast me away from your commandments.
I have hidden your words in my heart, so that I may not sin against you.
Blessed are you, Lord; teach me your statutes.
With my lips I have declared all the judgments of your mouth.
I have delighted in the way of your testimonies as in all riches.
I will meditate on your commandments and consider your ways.
I will study your statutes; I will not forget your words.
Deal generously with your servant; give me life, and I will keep your words.
Open my eyes, and I will understand the wonders of your law.
I am a stranger on earth; do not hide your commandments from me.
My soul has loved to long for your judgments at all times.
You have rebuked the proud; cursed are those who turn away from your commandments.
Take reproach and contempt away from me, for I have sought your testimonies.
For princes sat and spoke against me, but your servant meditated on your statutes.
For your testimonies are my study, and your statutes are my counselors.
My soul clings to the earth; give me life according to your word.
I declared my ways, and you heard me; teach me your statutes.
Teach me the way of your statutes, and I will meditate on your wonders.
My soul has fallen asleep from despondency; strengthen me in your words.
Remove the way of wrongdoing from me, and show me mercy through your law.
I have chosen the way of truth; I have not forgotten your judgments.
I have held fast to your testimonies, Lord; do not put me to shame.
I ran in the way of your commandments when you enlarged my heart.
Set the way of your statutes before me as a law, Lord, and I will seek it continually.
Give me understanding, and I will examine your law and keep it with all my heart.
Guide me on the path of your commandments, for I have desired it.
Incline my heart to your testimonies, and not to greed.
Turn my eyes away from looking at worthless things; give me life in your way.
Establish your word for your servant in the fear of you.
Take away the disgrace I feared, for your commands are good.
See, I have longed for your commandments; give me life in your righteousness.
And let your mercy come upon me, Lord, and your salvation according to your word.
I will answer those who insult me, for I have trusted in your words.
And do not take the word of truth entirely from my mouth, for I have placed my hope in your judgments.
And I will keep your law always, forever and ever.
And I walked in a spacious place, for I sought your commandments.
And I spoke of your testimonies before kings, and I was not ashamed.
And I meditated on your commandments, which I loved.
And I lifted my hands toward your commandments, which I loved, and I meditated on your statutes.
Remember your word to your servant, in which you have given me hope.
This comforted me in my humiliation: your word gave me life.
The proud transgressed the law greatly, but I did not turn aside from your law.
I remembered your judgments from of old, Lord, and I was comforted.
Sorrow seized me because of sinners who abandon your law.
Your statutes were songs to me in the place where I lived as a stranger.
I remembered your name in the night, Lord, and I kept your law.
This came to me because I sought your statutes.
You are my portion, Lord; I said that I would keep your law.
I prayed before your face with all my heart; have mercy on me according to your word.
I considered my ways and turned my feet toward your testimonies.
I prepared myself and was not troubled, so that I might keep your commandments.
The cords of sinners entangled me, but I did not forget your law.
At midnight I arose to give you thanks for your righteous judgments.
I am a companion of all who fear you and who keep your commandments.
The earth is full of your mercy, Lord; teach me your statutes.
You have dealt well with your servant, Lord, according to your word.
Teach me goodness, discipline, and understanding, for I have believed in your commandments.
Before I was humbled, I sinned; therefore I have kept your word.
You are good, Lord, and in your goodness teach me your statutes.
The injustice of the proud has multiplied against me, but I will study your commandments with all my heart.
Their hearts have curdled like milk, but I have meditated on your law.
It is good for me that you have humbled me, so that I may learn your statutes.
The law of your mouth is better to me than thousands of gold and silver pieces. GLORY.
Your hands made me and fashioned me; give me understanding, and I will learn your commandments.
Those who fear you will see me and rejoice, because I have put my hope in your words.
I know, Lord, that your decrees are righteous, and that in truth you have humbled me.
Let your mercy comfort me, according to your word to your servant.
Let your compassion come to me, and I will live, for your law is my meditation.
Let the proud be put to shame, because they have acted lawlessly against me without cause; but I will meditate on your commandments.
Let those who fear you turn to me, and those who know your testimonies.
Let my heart be blameless in your statutes, so that I may not be put to shame.
My soul wastes away longing for your salvation; I have put my hope in your words.
My eyes have grown weary looking for your word, as I say, “When will you comfort me?”
For I have become like a wineskin in the frost, yet I have not forgotten your statutes.
How many are the days of your servant? When will you pass judgment on those who persecute me?
Lawbreakers have told me idle tales, but they are not according to your law, Lord.
All your commandments are truth. They persecuted me unjustly; help me.
They almost destroyed me on earth, but I did not abandon your commandments.
Give me life according to your mercy, and I will keep the testimonies of your mouth.
Forever, O Lord, your word remains in heaven.
Your truth endures from generation to generation. You established the earth, and it remains.
By your decree the day continues, for all things serve you.
If your law had not been my meditation, I would have perished in my affliction. [?] Do not say after “O Lord,” after [?].
I will never forget your statutes, for through them you have given me life. Glory.
I am yours; save me, for I have sought your statutes.
Sinners lie in wait to destroy me, but I have understood your testimonies.
I have seen an end to every perfection, but your commandment is exceedingly broad.
How I have loved your law, O Lord! It is my meditation all day long.
You have made me wiser than my enemies through your commandment, for it is mine forever.
I have gained more understanding than all who study, for your testimonies are my meditation.
I have gained more understanding than the elders, for I have sought your commandments.
I have kept my feet from every evil path so that I may keep your words.
21. I have not turned aside from your judgments, for you have laid down the law for me.
How sweet your words are to my throat, sweeter than honey to my mouth!
Through your commandments I have gained understanding; therefore I have hated every unjust path.
Your law is a lamp for my feet and a light for my paths.
I have sworn and have not abandoned my pledge to keep your righteous judgments.
I have been greatly humbled, O Lord; give me life according to your word.
Accept the freewill offerings of my mouth, O Lord, and teach me your judgments.
My soul is always in your hands, and I have not forgotten your law.
Sinners have laid a snare for me, but I have not strayed from your commandments.
I have inherited your testimonies forever, for they are the joy of my heart.
Incline my heart to carry out your statutes forever, for the reward.
I have hated lawbreakers, but I have loved your law.
You are my helper and protector; I have placed my hope in your words.
Turn away from me, evildoers, and you who examine the commandments of my God.
Receive me according to your word, and I shall live; do not put me to shame in my hope.
Help me, Lord, and I shall be saved; I shall meditate on your statutes continually.
You have brought low all who stray from your statutes, for their thinking is unjust.
I have regarded all the sinners of the earth as transgressors; therefore I have loved your testimonies.
Nail my flesh fast with fear of you, for I have feared your commands.
I have practiced justice and righteousness; do not hand me over to those who wrong me.
Wait for your servant for his good; do not let the proud slander me.
My eyes have grown weary looking for your salvation and for the word of your righteousness.
Deal with your servant according to your mercy, and teach me your statutes.
I am your servant; give me understanding, and I shall know your testimonies, Lord.
It is time for the Lord to act; they have destroyed your law.
Therefore I have loved your commandments more than gold and topaz.
Therefore I have directed myself according to all your commandments; I have hated every unrighteous path.
Your testimonies are wonderful; therefore my soul has examined them.
The explanation of your words gives light and gives understanding to little children.
I opened my mouth and drew in breath, for I longed for your commandments. Glory.
Look upon me and have mercy on me, as you judge those who love your name.
Direct my steps according to your word, and let no lawlessness rule over me.
Deliver me from human slander, and I shall keep your commandments.
Make your face shine upon your servant, and teach me your statutes.
My eyes have poured out streams of water because I have not kept your law.
You are righteous, Lord, and your judgments are right.
You have commanded your decrees in righteousness and complete truth.
Zeal for you has consumed me, because my enemies have forgotten your words.
Your word is thoroughly refined, and your servant loves it.
I am young and despised, but I have not forgotten your statutes.
Your righteousness is everlasting righteousness, and your law is truth.
Trouble and distress have found me, but your commandments are my meditation.
Your decrees are righteous forever. Give me understanding, and I will live.
I cried out with all my heart; hear me, Lord. I will seek your statutes.
I cried out to you: Save me, and I will keep your decrees.
I rose before dawn and cried out; I placed my hope in your words.
My eyes were awake before morning, so that I might meditate on your words.
Hear my voice, Lord, according to your mercy; give me life according to your judgment.
Those who lawlessly persecute me have drawn near, but they have gone far from your law.
You are near, Lord, and all your ways are truth.
From the beginning I have known from your decrees that you established them forever.
Look upon my humiliation and rescue me, for I have not forgotten your law.
Plead my case and deliver me; give me life for the sake of your word.
Salvation is far from sinners, because they have not sought your statutes.
Your mercies are many, Lord; give me life according to your judgment.
Many persecute and oppress me, but I have not turned aside from your decrees.
I saw those who lacked understanding and wasted away, because they did not keep your words.
See how I have loved your commandments, Lord; in your mercy give me life.
The beginning of your words is truth, and all your righteous judgments endure forever.
Princes persecuted me without cause, and my heart did not fear your words.
I will rejoice in your words like someone who finds much spoil.
I hated injustice and found it abhorrent, but I loved your law.
Seven times a day I praised you for your righteous judgments.
Those who love your law have great peace, and nothing makes them stumble.
I waited for your salvation, Lord, and loved your commandments.
My soul kept your testimonies and loved them greatly.
I kept your commandments and your testimonies, for all my ways are before you, Lord.
Let my prayer come near before you, Lord; give me understanding according to your word.
Let my plea come before you, Lord; deliver me according to your word.
My lips will pour forth praise when you teach me your statutes.
My tongue will proclaim your words, for all your commandments are righteous.
Let your hand save me, for I have chosen your commandments.
I have loved your salvation, Lord, and your law is my meditation.
My soul will live and praise you, and your judgments will help me.
I have wandered like a lost sheep. Seek your servant, for I have not forgotten your commandments.
119. Glory. A Song of Ascents. When I was in distress, I cried out to the Lord, and he heard me.
Lord, deliver my soul from lying lips and from a deceitful tongue.
What will be given to you, or what will be added to you, against a deceitful tongue?
The sharpened arrows of a mighty man, with burning coals of the wilderness.
Woe is me [?], for my sojourn has been prolonged! I have settled in dark dwellings.
My soul has sojourned a long time. I was peaceful with those who hate peace.
When I spoke to them, they fought against me without cause.
120. A Song of Ascents.
I lifted my eyes to the mountains, from where my help will come.
My help comes from the Lord, who made heaven and earth.
Do not let your foot slip; may the one who guards you not slumber.
Look, the one who guards Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.
The Lord will guard you; the Lord is your shelter at your right hand.
The sun will not burn you by day, nor the moon by night.
The Lord will guard you from every evil; the Lord will guard your soul.
The Lord will guard your coming in and your going out, from now and forever.
121. A SONG OF ASCENTS.
I rejoiced at those who said to me, “Let us go to the house of the Lord.”
Our feet were standing in your courts, Jerusalem.
Jerusalem is being built as a city whose parts are joined together.
For there the tribes will go up, the tribes of the Lord, as a testimony to Israel, to give thanks to the name of the Lord.
For there thrones were set for judgment, thrones in the house of David.
Pray for the peace of Jerusalem and for prosperity for those who love you.
May there be peace within your defenses and prosperity within your fortified walls.
For the sake of my brothers and my neighbors, I spoke of peace for you.
For the sake of the house of the Lord our God, I sought your good.
A SONG OF ASCENTS.
I have lifted my eyes to you, who dwell in heaven.
Look, as the eyes of servants are on the hands of their masters, as the eyes of a maidservant are on the hands of her mistress, so our eyes are on the Lord our God until he has compassion on us.
Have mercy on us, Lord, have mercy on us, for we have been filled with contempt beyond measure.
Our soul has been filled to overflowing with the scorn of those who prosper and the contempt of the proud.
123. A SONG OF ASCENTS.
If the Lord had not been among us—let Israel now say—
if the Lord had not been among us when people rose up against us—
Then they would have swallowed us alive, when their fury raged against us; then the water would have drowned us.
Our soul passed through the torrent.
Then our soul passed through water that cannot be withstood.
Blessed is the Lord, who will not give us as prey to their teeth.
Our soul will escape like a bird from the snare of the hunters.
The snare was broken, and we were delivered.
22. Our help is in the name of the Lord, who made heaven and earth.
124. Glory. A Song of Ascents.
Those who trust in the Lord are like Mount Zion. The one who lives in Jerusalem will never be shaken.
Mountains surround it, and the Lord surrounds his people, from now and forever.
For the Lord will not leave the scepter of sinners over the allotted land of the righteous, so that the righteous do not stretch out their hands to wrongdoing.
Do good, Lord, to the good and to the upright in heart. But those who turn aside into crooked ways the Lord will lead away with those who do evil.
125. Peace upon Israel. A Song of Ascents.
When the Lord brought back the captives of Zion, we were like people who had been comforted.
Then our mouth will be filled with joy, and our tongue with gladness. Then they will say among the nations:
“The Lord has done great things for us.” The Lord has done great things for us; we were glad.
Bring back our captives, Lord, like a torrent in the south.
Those who sowed with tears will reap with joy.
They went along weeping as they scattered their seed. But they will surely return with joy, carrying their sheaves.
126. A Song of Ascents.
Unless the Lord builds the house,

those who build it have labored in vain. Unless the Lord guards the city, the watchman has kept watch in vain. It is in vain that you rise early. Rise after sitting down, you who eat the bread of suffering, when he gives sleep to his beloved.
Look, sons are an inheritance from the Lord; the fruit of the womb is a reward.
Like arrows in the hand of a mighty man, so are the sons of those driven out.
Blessed is the man who satisfies his desire with them. They will not be put to shame when they speak with their enemies at the gates.
127. A Song of Ascents.
Blessed are all who fear the Lord, who walk in his ways.
You will eat the fruit of your own labors. You are blessed, and it will go well with you.
Your wife will be like a fruitful, flourishing vine within your house. Your sons will be like young olive shoots around your table.
See, this is how the man who fears the Lord will be blessed.
May the Lord bless you from Zion, and may you see the good things of Jerusalem all the days of your life.
And may you see your sons’ sons. Peace upon Israel!
128. A Song of Ascents.
Many times they fought against me from my youth—let Israel now say—many times they fought, fought against me from my youth, for they have not overcome me.
Sinners hammered upon my back; they prolonged their lawlessness.
The Lord is righteous; he cut through the necks of sinners.
May all who hate Zion be put to shame and turned back.
May they be like grass on buildings, on rooftops, which withers before it is pulled up.
With it the reaper does not fill his hand, nor does the one gathering sheaves fill his lap.
And those passing by have not said, “The blessing of the Lord be upon you! We have blessed in the name of the Lord.”
Out of the depths I cried to you, Lord. Lord, hear my voice.
Let your ears be attentive to the voice of my prayer.
If you take account of lawless deeds, Lord, Lord, who will stand? For forgiveness comes from you.
For your name’s sake I have waited for you, Lord. My soul has waited for your word; my soul has hoped in the Lord.
From the morning watch until night, from the morning watch let Israel hope in the Lord.
For mercy comes from the Lord, and abundant redemption comes from him. And he will redeem Israel from all its lawless deeds.
130. A Song of Ascents.
And, Lord, my heart was not proud, nor were my eyes lifted high. I did not pursue great things or wonders beyond me.
If I was not humble, but exalted my soul, like a weaned child upon its mother, so will you repay my soul.
Let Israel hope in the Lord, from now and forever.
131. A Song of Ascents.
Remember, Lord, David and all his meekness.
How he swore to the Lord and made a vow to the God of Jacob:
“I will not enter the dwelling of my house or climb onto my bed,
or give sleep to my eyes, slumber to my eyelids, or rest to my temples,
until I find a place for the Lord, a dwelling for the God of Jacob.”
Look, we heard of it in Ephrathah; we found it in the fields of the forest.
Let us enter his dwelling; let us bow down at the place where his feet stood.
Arise, Lord, and enter your resting place, you and the ark of your holiness.
Your priests will be clothed in righteousness, and your faithful ones will rejoice.
For the sake of David your servant, do not turn away the face of your anointed one.
The Lord swore to David in truth, and he will not go back on it: “I will set one of the offspring of your body on your throne.
If your sons keep my covenant and these testimonies of mine that I will teach them, their sons too will sit on your throne forever.”
For the Lord chose Zion and desired it as his dwelling:
“This is my resting place forever and ever; here I will dwell, for I have desired it.
I will abundantly bless its widows; I will satisfy its poor with bread.
I will clothe its priests in salvation, and its faithful ones will rejoice with joy.
There I will make a horn sprout for David; I have prepared a lamp for my anointed one.
I will clothe his enemies in shame, but my holiness will flourish upon him.”
132. A Song of Ascents.
See how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to live together!
It is like anointing oil on the head, running down onto Aaron’s beard, running down onto the edges of his robe.
It is like the dew of Hermon descending upon the mountains of Zion. For there the Lord commanded the blessing: life forever.
133. A Song of Ascents.
Now bless the Lord, all you servants of the Lord, who stand in the Lord’s temple, in the court of the house of our God.
At night lift up your hands in the sanctuary, and bless the Lord.
May the Lord bless you from Zion, he who made heaven and earth.
134. Glory. [?] Alleluia.
Praise the name of the Lord; praise him, servants of the Lord,
you who stand in the temple of the Lord, in the court of the house of our God.
Praise the Lord, for the Lord is good; sing to his name, for it is good.
For the Lord has chosen Jacob for himself, Israel as his own possession.
For I know [?] that the Lord is great, and our God is above all gods.
Whatever the Lord wished, he did, in heaven and on earth, in the seas and in all the depths.
He raises clouds from the ends of the earth; he made lightning for the rain and brings winds out of his storehouses.
He struck down all the firstborn of Egypt, from human beings to livestock.
He sent signs and wonders into your midst, Egypt, against Pharaoh [?] and all his servants.
He struck down many nations and killed mighty kings:
Sihon [?], king of the Amorites, and all the kingdoms of Canaan.
And he gave their land as an inheritance, an inheritance to Israel, his people.
Lord, your name endures forever, and your remembrance from generation to generation.
For the Lord will judge his people and have compassion on his servants.
The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the work of human hands.
They have mouths but do not speak; they have eyes but do not see.
They have ears but do not hear, for there is no breath in their mouths.
May those who make them become like them, and all who trust in them.
House of Israel, bless the Lord; house of Aaron, bless the Lord.
House of Levi, bless the Lord; you who fear the Lord, bless the Lord.
Blessed be the Lord from Zion, he who dwells in Jerusalem.
135. Alleluia.
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever.
Give thanks to the God of gods, for his mercy endures forever. Give thanks to the Lord of lords, for his mercy endures forever.
To him who alone has done great wonders, for his mercy endures forever.
To him who made the heavens with understanding, for his mercy endures forever.
To him who established the earth upon the waters, for his mercy endures forever.
To him who alone made the great lights, for his mercy endures forever.
The sun to rule the day, for his mercy endures forever.
The moon and stars to rule the night, for his mercy endures forever.
To him who struck Egypt along with its firstborn, for his mercy endures forever.
And brought Israel out from among them, for his mercy endures forever.
With a mighty hand and an uplifted arm, for his mercy endures forever.
To him who divided the Red Sea into parts, for his mercy endures forever.
And led Israel through its midst, for his mercy endures forever.
And hurled Pharaoh and his army into the Red Sea, for his mercy endures forever.
And guided his people in the wilderness, for his mercy endures forever.
To him who alone struck down great kings, for his mercy endures forever.
And killed mighty kings, for his mercy endures forever.
Sihon, king of the Amorites, for his mercy endures forever.
And Og, king of Bashan, for his mercy endures forever.
And gave their land as an inheritance, for his mercy endures forever.
An inheritance to Israel his servant, for his mercy endures forever.
For the Lord remembered us in our lowly state, for his mercy endures forever.
And has delivered us from our enemies, for his mercy endures forever.
He who gives food to all flesh, for his mercy endures forever.
Give thanks to the God of heaven, for his mercy endures forever.
Psalm 136. Of David. By the river of Babylon, there we sat and wept as we remembered Zion.
On the willows in its midst we hung our instruments.
For there those who had captured us asked us, and those who had led us away asked for songs: “Sing us some of the songs of Zion.”
How shall we sing the Lord’s song in a foreign land?
If I forget you, Jerusalem, let my right hand be forgotten.
Let my tongue cling to my throat if I do not remember you, if I do not put Jerusalem first, as the beginning of my joy.
Remember, Lord, the sons of Edom on the day of Jerusalem, who said, “Tear it down, tear it down to its foundations!”
Wretched daughter of Babylon! Blessed is the one who repays you your repayment, which he will repay to us.
Blessed is the one who seizes your infants and smashes them against a stone.
137. Glory. Of David and Zechariah.
I will give thanks to you, Lord, with all my heart, and before the angels I will sing to you, because you have heard all the words of my mouth.
I will bow down toward your holy temple. I will give thanks to your name for your mercy and your truth, because your holy name has been magnified above all things.
On whatever day I call upon you, hear me quickly. You have increased my soul and my strength.
All the kings of the earth will give thanks to you, Lord, because they have heard all the words of my mouth.
And they will sing the songs of the Lord.
For great is the glory of the Lord. For the Lord is exalted and looks upon the humble, and he knows the lofty from afar.
If I walk in the midst of affliction, you will give me life. Against the wrath of my enemies he will stretch out your hand, and your right hand will save me.
The Lord will repay on my behalf. Lord, your mercy lasts forever. Do not disregard the works of your hands.
[?]. For the end. A psalm of David. Lord, you have tested me and known me.
You know my knowledge and my rising. You understand my thoughts from afar.
You have searched out my path and my untrodden way, and you have examined all my ways.
For there is no deceit on my tongue.
See, Lord, you know all my later things and my earlier things. You created me and laid your hand upon me.
Your knowledge concerning me has become wondrous. It has grown mighty, and I cannot reach it.
Where shall I go from your Spirit? And where shall I flee from your presence?
If I ascend into heaven, you are there. If I descend into Hades, you are there.
If I take my wings and settle at the farthest reaches of the sea,
even there your hand will guide me, and your right hand will hold me.
And I said, “Surely darkness will trample me down, and night will be illumination for my food.”
For its darkness will not be dark to you, and night will shine like day. Its darkness and its light are alike.
For you possessed my inward parts. You received me from my mother’s womb.
I will give thanks to you, for I was fearfully amazed. Your works are wonderful, and my soul knows them very well.
My bones were not hidden from you, which you made in secret, nor my substance in the lowest parts of the earth.
Your eyes saw my unformed being, and all will be written in your books. They will be formed by day, and there is no one among them.
But your friends were greatly honored by me, O God. Their beginnings became very strong.
I will count them, and they will outnumber the sand. I arose, and I am with you again.
If you kill the sinners, O God! Men of blood, turn away from me.
If you speak in your thoughts, they will take your cities in vain.
Did I not hate those who hate you, O Lord? And I wasted away over your enemies.
I hated them with complete hatred. They became my enemies.
Test me, O Lord, and understand my heart. Examine me and know my paths.
And see whether there is a way of lawlessness in me, and guide me on the everlasting way.
[?]. For the end. A psalm of David.
Rescue me, O Lord, from an evil person; deliver me from an unjust man.
They devised injustice in their hearts. All day long they prepared for war.
They sharpened their tongues like a serpent’s. The venom of asps is under their lips. Interlude.
Keep me, O Lord, from the hand of the sinner. Rescue me from an unjust person, from those who planned to trip my feet.
The proud hid a snare for me, and with ropes they stretched out a net for my feet. Beside the path they set a trap for me.
I said to the Lord, “You are my God.” Listen, O Lord, to my prayer.
O Lord, Lord, the strength of my salvation, you have sheltered my head on the day of battle.
Do not hand me over, Lord, because of my desire, to the sinner. They have plotted against me; do not abandon me, lest he exalt himself. Interlude.
As for the head of those who surround them, the trouble caused by their lips will cover them.
Coals will fall upon them. Cast them down with fire. They will not stand amid sufferings. Interlude.
A man of many words will not prosper on earth. Evils will hunt down an unjust man to his destruction.
I know that the Lord will secure justice for the needy and vindication for the poor.
Surely the righteous will give thanks to your name, and the upright will rejoice in your presence. Glory.
[?]. A psalm of David. Lord, I have cried out to you; hear me. Attend to the voice of my prayer when I cry out to you.
Let my prayer be set before you like incense, the lifting of my hands like an evening sacrifice.
Set a guard over my mouth, Lord, and a secure door over my lips.
Do not incline my heart toward deceitful words, to make excuses for sins together with people who practice lawlessness. And they will not associate with their chosen ones.
A righteous man will correct me mercifully and rebuke me. But let the oil of a sinner not anoint my head, for my prayer is still amid good pleasures.
Their judges were swallowed up beside the rock. My words will be heard, for I will prevail.
Like a clod of earth split apart on the ground, their bones were scattered beside Hades.
For my eyes are turned toward you, Lord, Lord. I have put my hope in you; do not take away my life.
Keep me from the snare they have set for me and from the traps of those who practice lawlessness.
Sinners will fall into their own net. I am alone until I pass through.
121. An instruction of David. A prayer when he was in the cave.
With my voice I cried out to the Lord; with my voice I pleaded with the Lord.
I will pour out my prayer before him; I declared my distress before him.
When my spirit was failing within me, he knew my paths. On this road along which I was walking, they hid a snare for me.
I looked to the right and watched, but there was no one who knew me. Escape failed me, and there is no one who cares for my life.
I cried out to you, Lord; I said, “You are my hope; you are my portion in the land of the living.”
Attend to my prayer, for I have been brought very low. Deliver me from those who pursue me, for they have become stronger than I.
And bring my soul out of prison, so that I may give thanks to you, to your name. The righteous are waiting for me until you reward me.
[?]. A psalm of David, when his son Absalom was pursuing him. Lord, hear my prayer. Listen to my plea in your truth; hear me in your righteousness.
Do not enter into judgment with your servant, for no living person will be justified before you.
For the enemy has pursued my soul; he has brought my life down to the ground. He has made me sit in darkness like those long dead.
My spirit grew faint within me; my heart was troubled within me.
I remembered the days of old. I meditated on all your deeds; I reflected on the works of your hands.
I stretched out my hands to you. My soul is like a waterless land before you.
Answer me quickly, Lord; my spirit is failing. Do not turn your face away from me, or I will become like those who go down into the pit.
Let me hear of your mercy in the morning, for I have put my hope in you. Show me, Lord, the way I should go, for I have lifted up my soul to you.
Rescue me from my enemies, Lord; I have fled to you for refuge.
Teach me to do your will, for you are my God. Your good Spirit will guide me onto level ground.
For your name’s sake, Lord, you will preserve my life. In your righteousness you will bring my soul out of distress.
In your mercy you will destroy my enemies and put an end to all who oppress my soul, for I am your servant. Glory. Sessional hymn.
PSALM 122. OF DAVID, AGAINST GOLIATH. Blessed is the Lord my God, who trains my hands for battle and my fingers for war.
My mercy and my refuge, my protector and my deliverer, my helper in whom I have put my hope, who subjects my people to me.
Lord, what is a human being, that you have made yourself known to him, or a son of man, that you take account of him?
A human being has become like a breath; his days pass away like a shadow.
Lord, bend down the heavens and come down. Touch your mountains, and they will smoke.
Flash your lightning, and you will scatter them. Send out your arrows, and you will throw them into confusion.
Send your hand from above and rescue me.
And their right hand is a right hand of falsehood.
God, I will sing a new song to you; on a ten-stringed harp I will sing to you.
To you who give victory to kings, who rescue David your servant from the cruel sword.
And their right hand is a right hand of falsehood.
Their sons are like young shoots, firmly rooted in their youth. Their daughters are adorned and embellished like the ornamentation of a temple.
Their storehouses are full, overflowing with one thing after another. Their sheep are prolific, multiplying in their pastures.
Their oxen are fat. There is no downfall or outcry in their streets.
They have called the people who have these things blessed. Blessed are the people whose God is the Lord.
Psalm 123. Of David. I will exalt you, my God, my King, and bless your name forever and ever.
Every day I will bless you and praise your name forever and ever.
Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised, and his greatness has no end.
Generation after generation will praise your works and proclaim your power.
They will speak of the splendor of the glory of your holiness and recount your wonders.
They will speak of the power of your fearsome deeds and recount your greatness.
They will cast aside the memory of your abundant goodness and rejoice in your righteousness.
The Lord is compassionate and merciful, patient and most merciful.
The Lord is good to all, and his compassion rests upon all his works.
All your works will give thanks to you, Lord, and your faithful ones will bless you.
They will speak of the glory of your kingdom and tell of your power,
to make your power known to the children of men, and the glory of the splendor of your kingdom.
Your kingdom is a kingdom for all ages, and your dominion endures through every generation. The Lord is faithful in all his words and holy in all his works.
The Lord supports all who are falling and raises up all who have been cast down.
The eyes of all look to you in hope, and you give them their food at the proper time.
You open your hand and satisfy every living creature with your favor.
The Lord is righteous in all his ways and holy in all his works.
He will fulfill the wishes of those who fear him, hear their prayer, and save them.
The Lord guards all who love him, but he will destroy all sinners.
My mouth will speak the praise of the Lord, and let all flesh bless his holy name. Glory.
124. Alleluia. Of Haggai and Zechariah. Praise the Lord, my soul.
I will praise the Lord throughout my life; I will sing to my God as long as I exist.
Do not put your trust in princes or in the sons of men, in whom there is no salvation.
His spirit will depart, and he will return to his earth. On that day all their thoughts will perish.
Blessed is the one whose helper is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the Lord his God.
Who made heaven and earth, the sea and everything in them, who keeps truth forever.
Who gives justice to the oppressed, who gives food to the hungry. The Lord frees those in chains.
The Lord gives wisdom to the blind. The Lord raises up those who have been cast down. The Lord loves the righteous.
The Lord protects foreigners. He takes in the orphan and the widow, and he destroys the ways of sinners.
The Lord will reign forever, your God, Zion, from generation to generation.
ALLELUIA. OF HAGGAI AND ZECHARIAH. Praise the Lord, for a psalm is good; let praise be pleasing to our God.
The Lord builds Jerusalem. He will gather the scattered people of Israel.
He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.
He counts the multitude of stars and calls them all by name.
Great is our Lord, and great is his strength. His understanding has no limit.
The Lord lifts up the meek, but brings sinners down to the ground.
Sing to our God with lyres.
Who covers heaven with clouds, who prepares rain for the earth, who makes grass grow on the mountains and plants for human use.
Who gives the livestock their food, and the young ravens that call upon him.
He takes no pleasure in the strength of a horse, nor does he delight in the legs of a man.
The Lord delights in those who fear him and those who hope in his mercy.
127. ALLELUIA. OF HAGGAI AND ZECHARIAH. Praise the Lord, Jerusalem. Praise your God, Zion.
For he has strengthened the bars of your gates. He has blessed your children within you.
He establishes peace within your borders and satisfies you with the finest wheat.
He sends his word to the earth. His word runs swiftly.
Who gives his snow like wool, who scatters mist like ashes.
Who casts his ice like loaves of bread. Who can stand before his frost?
He will send his word and melt them. His breath will blow, and the waters will flow.
He declares his word to Jacob, his decrees and judgments to Israel.
He has not done this for any other nation, nor has he made his judgments known to them. GLORY.
ALLELUIA. OF HAGGAI AND ZECHARIAH. Praise the Lord from the heavens; praise him in the heights.
Praise him, all his angels; praise him, all his hosts.
Praise him, sun and moon; praise him, all stars and light.
Praise him, heavens of heavens, and waters above the heavens.
Let them praise the name of the Lord, for he spoke, and they came into being; he commanded, and they were created.
He established them forever and ever. He laid down a command, and they will not transgress it.
Praise the Lord from the earth, sea monsters and all the depths,
fire, hail, snow, ice, and stormy wind, which carry out his word;
mountains and all hills, fruit trees and all cedars;
wild animals and all livestock, creeping creatures and winged birds;
kings of the earth and all peoples, princes and all judges of the earth;
young men and maidens, old men together with children.
Let them praise the name of the Lord, for his name alone is exalted.
And he will raise up the horn of his people, a song of praise for all his faithful ones, for the children of Israel, the people who draw near to him.
ALLELUIA. Sing a new song to the Lord, his praise in the assembly of his faithful ones.
Let Israel rejoice in his maker, and let the children of Zion rejoice in their king.
Let them praise your name with dancing; let them sing to him with tambourine and harp.
For the Lord takes pleasure in his people, and he will exalt the meek through salvation.
The faithful will exult in glory and rejoice on their beds.
The praises of God are in their throats, and double-edged swords are in their hands,
to take vengeance on the nations and bring rebukes upon the peoples,
to bind their kings with fetters and their nobles with iron handcuffs,
to carry out upon them the judgment that is written. This glory belongs to all his faithful ones.
ALLELUIA. Praise God among his holy ones; praise him in the firmament of his power.
Praise him for his mighty deeds. Praise him according to his surpassing greatness.
Praise him with the sound of the trumpet. Praise him with the psaltery and harp.
Praise him with the tambourine and dancing. Praise him with strings and pipe.
Praise him with sweet-sounding cymbals. Praise him with resounding cymbals.
Let everything that breathes praise the Lord.

Glory. Books. A psalm of David. This psalm is David’s own and is outside the numbering. When he went out to battle against Goliath. I was the smallest among my brothers and the youngest in my father’s house. I tended my father’s sheep.
My hands made musical instruments; my fingers fashioned a psaltery.
And who will tell my Lord? The Lord himself heard me.
And he sent his angel and anointed me with the mercy of anointing. And he took me away from my father’s sheep.
My brothers were handsome and tall, but the Lord did not favor them.
I went out to face the foreigner, and he cursed me by his idols.
But I drew his sword and beheaded him, and removed the disgrace from the children of Israel.
